algorithm.title: Diagnostic 2x2 table calculations

nodes.text: Set up 2x2 contingency table: disease status (columns) vs test results (rows)
Prevalence: total diseased / total population = 100 / 1000 = 10%
**Sensitivity (true positive rate):** TP / (TP + FN) = 70 / 100 = 70%
**Specificity (true negative rate):** TN / (TN + FP) = 720 / 900 = 80%
**Positive predictive value (PPV):** TP / (TP + FP) = 70 / 250 = 28%
**Negative predictive value (NPV):** TN / (TN + FN) = 720 / 750 = 96%
Remember: sensitivity and specificity are intrinsic to test; PPV and NPV depend on prevalence

nodes.text: Classify fetal heart rate tracing into three standardized NICHD categories
**Category I (normal):** baseline 110-160, moderate variability (6-25 bpm), no late/variable decels, accelerations present/absent

**Category II (indeterminate):** tachycardia, minimal variability, or recurrent variable decels (requires intrauterine resuscitation)
**Category III (abnormal):** absent variability with recurrent late decels, recurrent variable decels, bradycardia, or sinusoidal pattern
**Action for Category III:** immediate intrauterine resuscitation; emergent operative delivery if unresolved

algorithm.title: Randomized clinical trial validity and analytic strategies

nodes.text: Randomized clinical trials: randomization balances known and unknown confounding variables across comparison groups
Intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis: analyze all patients in assigned randomized groups regardless of protocol deviations or dropout
Per-protocol analysis: analyzes only participants completing intervention as planned, risking severe attrition bias
**Excluding perioperative surgical deaths:** severely violates ITT and falsely inflates surgical treatment efficacy
As-treated analysis: categorizes patients by intervention received, eliminating benefits of baseline randomization
Sensitivity analyses: report both ITT and per-protocol results to assess robustness of findings

abdominal-wall-disorders.scope: Rectus sheath hematoma, Fothergill sign, epigastric hernia, umbilical hernia, incisional hernia, diastasis recti
abdominal-wall-disorders.core: A focal abdominal-wall mass or pain persisting with muscle contraction suggests a wall lesion rather than visceral disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Anticoagulation, severe cough, pregnancy, trauma → rectus bleeding
Prior laparotomy, obesity, wound infection → incisional defect; increased intra-abdominal pressure promotes hernias

items: Epigastric vessel or muscle injury → blood confined within rectus sheath
Fascial defect permits fat/bowel protrusion; linea alba stretching separates rectus muscles in diastasis

★ Suspected hematoma → **CBC, coagulation studies, CT**; contrast identifies active extravasation

★ Hemodynamic instability → resuscitation/transfusion; persistent arterial bleeding → **embolization**
Strangulated or obstructed hernia → urgent operation; avoid forceful reduction

Hernia → bowel ischemia/perforation; repair → infection or recurrence

acid-base-disorders.name: Acid-base disorders
acid-base-disorders.scope: Metabolic acidosis (anion gap, non-anion gap), metabolic alkalosis (saline-responsive vs saline-resistant), respiratory acidosis, respiratory alkalosis, Winter formula, mixed disorders
acid-base-disorders.core: Identify the primary pH disturbance, test expected compensation, then investigate the anion gap or urine chloride to locate the cause.

rows.label: Definition
items: Acidemia: pH <7.35; alkalemia: >7.45; normal pH can hide opposing primary disorders
Metabolic: primary HCO3 change; respiratory: primary PaCO2 change

rows.label: Formula
items: ★ **AG = Na − (Cl + HCO3)**; usual normal ≈8–12, laboratory dependent
Hypoalbuminemia correction: add 2.5 to AG per 1 g/dL albumin below 4
★ **Winter: expected PaCO2 = 1.5 × HCO3 + 8 ±2**

rows.label: Interpret
items: HCO3 12 → expected PaCO2 26 ±2; measured 40 → additional respiratory acidosis
Metabolic alkalosis: expected PaCO2 ≈40 + 0.7 × (HCO3 − 24), ±5
Respiratory HCO3 change per 10 PaCO2: acidosis +1 acute/+4 chronic; alkalosis −2 acute/−4 chronic

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Alkalosis: **urine Cl <20 mmol/L** → saline-responsive; ≥20 → diuretics/mineralocorticoids
ΔAG exceeds HCO3 fall → additional alkalosis; smaller ΔAG → additional non-gap acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Compensation never overshoots; values outside expected range imply **mixed disorder**
Salicylates often cause respiratory alkalosis plus high-gap acidosis; near-normal pH is deceptive
Diarrhea/RTA: non-gap acidosis; distal RTA: urine pH >5.5, hypokalemia; renal failure: either gap pattern

acid-base-disorders.evidence: Established physiologic formulas; no guideline involved.

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, cirrhosis, low-output heart failure (prerenal despite overload); baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment (dipstick blood, few RBCs), prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → tubulointerstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**
Anuria despite patent catheter after pelvic surgery + hydronephrosis → ureteral injury/ligation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia (postoperative oliguria, high urine specific gravity) → saline bolus; congestion → loop diuretic; no reflex fluids in overload
Stop nephrotoxins, all NSAIDs including celecoxib (intra-articular steroid for joint pain); persistent AIN → glucocorticoids; renal-dose drugs
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function
Contrast in high-risk CKD → **periprocedural IV isotonic saline**; diuretics, mannitol, metformin stop don't protect
ACR now limits contrast prophylaxis mainly to eGFR <30; older exam questions may expect wider hydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

Mandatory reporting thresholds for consensual sexual activity depend on ages and local law
Disclose minimum necessary information; explain safety-driven disclosure to adolescent whenever feasible

adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics principles; jurisdiction-specific consent/reporting law must be verified locally.

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all 19–59; ≥60 with risk/request; health worker anti-HBs negative post-series → revaccinate
**HIV any CD4**, liver disease/alcohol, COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal <50; liver → HepA/HepB
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Anti-HBs/anti-HAV/VZV IgG positive → immune, skip; otherwise **do not delay vaccination** for serology
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza**: severe immunosuppression, pregnancy (nonimmune → postpartum)
PCV15 → PPSV23: ≥8 weeks immunocompromised; older exams: PPSV23 alone; mild illness/antibiotics: no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern; inactivated influenza cannot cause flu, coincidental virus; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

advance-directives-and-surrogates.name: Advance directives and surrogate decisions
advance-directives-and-surrogates.scope: Living will, DNR/DNI orders, health care proxy, substituted judgment, best interests, advance care planning
advance-directives-and-surrogates.core: Follow the capable patient's current wishes; when capacity is absent, use valid directives and authorized surrogate judgment.

rows.label: Principle
items: Autonomy persists after incapacity through documented preferences and legally authorized decision-makers
Substituted judgment: patient's known values; best interests: benefits/burdens when preferences unknown

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Confirm capacity, directive validity, clinical applicability, and designated **health care proxy**
★ Apply the patient's instructions over conflicting surrogate preferences
Discuss goals, code status, surrogate early; terminal sole caregiver → plan **child guardianship**

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ **DNR limits CPR**; do not automatically withhold antibiotics, analgesia, nutrition, or other treatment
Dementia diagnosis, mild test errors, or disagreement ≠ incapacity; capacity is decision-specific
★ **Surrogate cannot compel contraindicated treatment** → withhold it; ethics consult unnecessary

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Capable patient may revise prior instructions; current informed choices control
No directive/proxy → adult next of kin; none eligible (minor relative) → **court guardian**
Clear directive/reported wishes/proxy–team agreement → no consult; unresolved conflict → ethics, court

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **DNI and DNR differ**; clarify acceptable ventilation and perioperative plans
Proxy needs no terminal illness; dementia tube-feeding request → review lack of benefit, harms
Surrogate conveys patient's known wishes, not own beliefs; missing paperwork doesn't block them

table.title: Documents and authority
rows: Durable health care power of attorney
Current medical order limiting specified intervention
Portable treatment orders for serious illness

advance-directives-and-surrogates.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics framework; document validity and surrogate hierarchy depend on jurisdiction.

alcohol-use-disorder.name: Alcohol use disorder
alcohol-use-disorder.scope: Unhealthy alcohol use, CAGE and AUDIT screening, transaminitis (AST > ALT), motivational interviewing, naltrexone, acamprosate
alcohol-use-disorder.core: Compulsive alcohol use despite harm, impaired control, or physiologic dependence calls for nonjudgmental assessment and relapse-prevention treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, early initiation, trauma, depression, anxiety, social stress
Binge drinking and escalating tolerance; coexisting sedative use increases overdose risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Craving, failed attempts to cut down, role impairment, continued use despite consequences
AST:ALT ≥1.5–2, macrocytosis, elevated GGT support exposure but neither prove nor exclude disorder
★ Tremor, tachycardia, hallucinations, seizures after reduction → **withdrawal**, potentially fatal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Chronic GABA enhancement/NMDA inhibition → compensatory adaptation; cessation unmasks CNS excitation
Mesolimbic reinforcement and stress circuitry sustain compulsive use and relapse

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Screen adults using **AUDIT-C** or single-question heavy-use screen; positive result → fuller assessment
DSM-5: ≥2 of 11 criteria within 12 months; 2–3 mild, 4–5 moderate, ≥6 severe
CAGE: Cut down, Annoyed, Guilty, Eye-opener; ≥2 positive suggests problem use, misses early risky drinking
Assess suicidality, other drugs, liver disease, nutritional deficiency, pregnancy, withdrawal history
Depression or major life stressor → always ask about alcohol use

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Motivational interviewing**: elicit goals, reflect ambivalence, agree achievable change; CBT and mutual support
Withdrawal → benzodiazepines; inpatient detoxification for severe history, unstable comorbidity, or unreliable support
Thiamine promptly for malnutrition/Wernicke risk; never delay emergency glucose for hypoglycemia
Disulfiram: selected supervised abstinence; avoid severe liver/cardiac disease; alcohol exposure causes aversive reaction

rows.label: Complications
items: Cirrhosis, pancreatitis, cardiomyopathy, neuropathy, cancer, injuries, fetal alcohol effects
Wernicke encephalopathy → Korsakoff amnesia; depression and suicide risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Ongoing **relapse planning**, frequent follow-up, social support; abstinence for pregnancy or advanced liver disease
Assess hepatitis vaccination, nutrition, driving safety, medication interactions
Asymptomatic AST>ALT transaminitis (<500, unlike viral >1000) in daily drinker → reversible with abstinence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sedative withdrawal: similar autonomic excitation with benzodiazepine/barbiturate reduction
Hyperthyroidism: tremor/tachycardia without alcohol-linked time course

table.title: Relapse prevention
rows: Current opioids; acute hepatitis/severe hepatic failure

alcohol-use-disorder.evidence: Not checked online; established screening and addiction-treatment principles.

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

table.title: Primary amenorrhea: high FSH or absent uterus → karyotype

amniotic-fluid-disorders.name: Amniotic fluid disorders
amniotic-fluid-disorders.scope: Oligohydramnios (AFI <= 5 cm or single deepest pocket < 2 cm, renal anomalies, uteroplacental insufficiency), polyhydramnios (AFI >= 24 cm, maternal diabetes, GI atresia, twin-twin transfusion syndrome, anencephaly)
amniotic-fluid-disorders.core: Amniotic fluid reflects fetal urine production and swallowing; abnormal volume directs evaluation toward membrane rupture, placental disease, or fetal anomalies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low fluid: PPROM, post-term pregnancy, maternal vascular disease, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs
High fluid: maternal diabetes, esophageal/duodenal atresia, anencephaly, fetal anemia; many mild cases idiopathic
Monochorionic twins: donor oligohydramnios and recipient polyhydramnios suggest twin-twin transfusion

rows.label: Clues
items: Fundal height smaller/larger than dates; fluid extremes may alter fetal movement perception
Severe excess → maternal dyspnea, distended tense abdomen; low volume → recurrent variable decelerations

rows.label: Pathophys
items: After midgestation, urine supplies most fluid; swallowing removes it
Placental hypoperfusion or absent kidneys reduces input; impaired swallowing or osmotic diuresis increases volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ultrasound fluid measurement** plus anatomy survey; single deepest pocket reduces oligohydramnios overdiagnosis
Low volume → sterile speculum examination for rupture, assess kidneys/bladder, growth and umbilical Doppler
High volume → diabetes testing, detailed fetal anatomy; evaluate anemia/infection when suggested

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Isolated persistent oligohydramnios → surveillance and delivery at **36–37+6 weeks**, or diagnosis thereafter
Low fluid from PPROM/FGR → manage underlying cause; intrapartum recurrent variables may benefit from amnioinfusion
★ Polyhydramnios with severe dyspnea/discomfort → **amnioreduction**; indomethacin not solely for fluid reduction
Severe polyhydramnios, mild symptoms → **serial antenatal fetal testing**; no routine amnioreduction
Mild idiopathic polyhydramnios → spontaneous term labor; elective induction no earlier than 39 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Early prolonged severe low fluid → pulmonary hypoplasia, limb contractures; later → cord compression
Excess fluid → preterm labor, malpresentation, prolapsed cord, abruption after decompression, postpartum atony

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Optimize glucose control; avoid **ACE inhibitors** and nonessential NSAIDs during pregnancy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Macrosomia: large fundal height but normal fluid measurement
Incorrect dating: size discrepancy without true volume abnormality

amniotic-fluid-disorders.evidence: Polyhydramnios checked 2026-10-30: [SMFM Consult 46](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30048635/); oligohydramnios timing follows established ACOG guidance.

anaphylaxis.name: Anaphylaxis
anaphylaxis.scope: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, biphasic reactions, epinephrine autoinjector, emergency airway management
anaphylaxis.core: Rapid multisystem reaction after exposure—or isolated hypotension or airway compromise after a known allergen—requires epinephrine immediately.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Foods, insect venom, antibiotics, latex; exercise can amplify food-triggered reactions
Asthma, prior severe reaction, mast-cell disorders; beta-blockers can complicate treatment

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Urticaria/angioedema + wheeze, stridor, hypotension, or severe GI symptoms**
Skin findings may be absent; hoarseness and tongue swelling predict airway danger
Biphasic recurrence after apparent resolution, especially after severe or undertreated episodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mast-cell/basophil mediators → vasodilation, capillary leak, bronchoconstriction; often IgE-mediated
Epinephrine: α1 reverses vasodilation/edema, β2 reverses bronchoconstriction; albuterol alone misses edema and shock

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; never wait for tryptase or laboratory confirmation
Acute and baseline serum tryptase can support uncertain cases; normal results do not exclude anaphylaxis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IM epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg**, adult 0.3–0.5 mg, lateral thigh; repeat every 5–15 minutes
Supine with legs elevated unless respiratory distress; oxygen, early intubation for progressive obstruction
Profound shock or refractory hypotension → titrated IV epinephrine plus **isotonic boluses**; beta-blocker use → glucagon
Albuterol for residual bronchospasm; antihistamines relieve itching only; steroids do not reliably prevent biphasic reactions
★ Monitor until resolved; **longer observation/admission** after hypotension, repeated epinephrine, or severe asthma

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxia, distributive shock, arrhythmia, hypoxic brain injury
Undiluted IV epinephrine bolus errors → ischemia and dangerous dysrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prescribe **epinephrine autoinjector**, demonstrate technique, provide written action plan and allergy referral
Extra device for repeat-dose risk; avoidance, medical alert ID; venom immunotherapy after qualifying sting allergy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal episode: bradycardia, pallor, rapid improvement supine
Bradykinin angioedema: no itching/hives; ACE inhibitor or hereditary disease → airway, icatibant/C1 inhibitor

angioedema.name: Angioedema
angioedema.scope: Hereditary angioedema (C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency, C4 level), ACE inhibitor-induced, mast cell-mediated vs bradykinin-mediated, acute airway compromise, C1-INH concentrate, icatibant
angioedema.core: Deep, transient swelling of lips, tongue, airway, or bowel; distinguishing histamine from bradykinin determines which drugs will work.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Allergens, NSAIDs, insect stings → mast cell activation
Hereditary attacks: autosomal dominant history, trauma, dental procedures, estrogen exposure
ACE inhibitors: attacks possible even after years of uneventful use

rows.label: Clues
items: Nonpitting, asymmetric edema; gastrointestinal attacks may cause severe colicky pain, vomiting
★ Hoarseness, stridor, drooling, rapidly progressive tongue swelling → **airway emergency**
Recurrent episodes beginning in childhood support hereditary disease; late onset suggests acquired deficiency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Histamine increases vascular permeability through mast cell mediator release
C1-INH deficiency/dysfunction or impaired bradykinin breakdown → kallikrein-mediated vascular leakage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Recurrent nonurticarial attacks → **C4 plus C1-INH level and function**; repeat abnormal results
Low C1-INH quantity → type I; normal/high quantity with low function → type II
Normal C4 does not fully exclude HAE; C1q low in acquired, usually normal in hereditary disease
ACE inhibitor-related disease: clinical diagnosis; complement usually normal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Secure threatened airway early with expert intubation; prepare surgical airway
Uncertain mechanism with possible anaphylaxis → IM epinephrine immediately; do not await complement testing
★ ACE inhibitor-related: stop drug permanently; airway/supportive care; targeted drug evidence inconsistent
HAE attack: give available on-demand drug early; plasma if specific agents unavailable

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxiation, hypovolemia from bowel edema; unnecessary abdominal surgery after misdiagnosis
Recurrence may continue after ACE inhibitor discontinuation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ HAE: on-demand rescue supply; procedure prophylaxis with C1-INH; avoid ACE inhibitors and estrogen
Frequent HAE attacks → lanadelumab, berotralstat, or scheduled C1-INH; screen first-degree relatives

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: persistent warm, tender erythema with infection signs
Contact dermatitis: superficial pruritic, eczematous eruption rather than isolated deep swelling

table.title: Mediator guides treatment
rows: Epinephrine for anaphylaxis; H1 antihistamine adjunct

anorectal-disorders.name: Anorectal disorders
anorectal-disorders.scope: Anal fissure, internal and external hemorrhoids, anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, pruritus ani, topical vasodilators, fiber, sitz baths
anorectal-disorders.core: Anal pain, bleeding, swelling, or drainage requires inspection and focused examination; pain pattern distinguishes fissure, thrombosis, and infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constipation, straining, pregnancy, prolonged sitting; Crohn disease, diabetes, immunosuppression increase infection risk
Irritant soaps, moisture, fecal seepage contribute to pruritus ani

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pain out of proportion, fever, spreading erythema, crepitus** → evaluate necrotizing perineal infection urgently
Posterior midline fissure common; lateral/multiple fissures suggest Crohn disease, infection, or malignancy
Internal hemorrhoids lie above dentate line; prolapse may require manual reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fissure causes internal sphincter spasm and local ischemia; hemorrhoids represent enlarged vascular cushions
Cryptoglandular infection creates abscess; persistent epithelialized tract can become a fistula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Inspection first**, gentle DRE/anoscopy when tolerable; do not force painful fissure examination
Deep pain without visible lesion → CT/MRI for occult abscess; recurrent fistula → pelvic MRI
Rectal bleeding with anemia, weight loss, bowel change, or screening indication → colon evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Fiber, fluids, stool softening, **sitz baths**; fissure → topical anesthetic, nitroglycerin or diltiazem
Refractory chronic fissure → botulinum toxin or lateral internal sphincterotomy after continence-risk assessment
Internal hemorrhoids persisting despite conservative measures → rubber-band ligation; advanced prolapse → surgery
★ Abscess → **incision and drainage**; antibiotics added for cellulitis, systemic illness, or immunosuppression
Fistula → colorectal surgery; painful thrombosed external hemorrhoid within 72 hours → consider excision

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess recurrence, fistula, sepsis; sphincter injury → fecal incontinence
Chronic bleeding → iron deficiency; pruritus → excoriations and secondary infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid straining and prolonged toilet sitting; gentle cleansing, dry skin, barrier ointment for seepage

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anal cancer: persistent irregular ulcer/mass or large wart-like lesion, biopsy required
Proctitis: urgency, tenesmus, mucous discharge
Pinworm: nocturnal itch, especially children; tape test

table.title: Local patterns
rows: Tearing defecation pain; bright blood on paper
Recurrent purulent drainage from external opening

anorectal-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established colorectal teaching.

anticoagulants.name: Anticoagulants
anticoagulants.scope: Warfarin (CYP interactions, INR monitoring, reversal with vitamin K and PCC), heparin and LMWH (protamine reversal, HIT), direct oral anticoagulants (apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, reversal agents)
anticoagulants.core: Anticoagulants prevent clot extension and embolization; drug choice depends on indication, renal function, pregnancy, and bleeding risk.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ **DOACs**: most nonvalvular AF and VTE; warfarin: mechanical valves, rheumatic mitral stenosis
LMWH: pregnancy; UFH: rapid reversibility or severe renal impairment

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Warfarin blocks vitamin K recycling → ↓II, VII, IX, X and proteins C/S
UFH/LMWH enhance antithrombin; UFH inhibits IIa/Xa, LMWH predominantly Xa
Apixaban/rivaroxaban directly inhibit Xa; dabigatran directly inhibits thrombin

rows.label: Adverse
items: Bleeding with all; warfarin → early skin necrosis, fetal injury
★ **HIT**: platelet fall >50%, usually days 5–10; thrombosis more characteristic than bleeding
High INR + bowel obstruction, hemoglobin drop → **intramural small-bowel hematoma**

rows.label: Avoid
items: Suspected HIT → stop every heparin source; start argatroban or another nonheparin anticoagulant
Warfarin initiation during acute HIT; DOACs for mechanical valves or high-risk antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Interactions
items: Warfarin ↑: amiodarone, TMP-SMX/metronidazole, **fluoroquinolones**; ↓: rifampin, vitamin K-rich diet
DOAC exposure altered by strong P-glycoprotein/CYP3A modifiers; NSAIDs/antiplatelets increase bleeding

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Warfarin **INR**, usually 2–3; UFH aPTT/anti-Xa; LMWH/DOACs: renal function, CBC
No routine INR titration for DOACs; LMWH anti-Xa only selected situations

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Acute VTE warfarin → overlap parenteral anticoagulant ≥5 days and until therapeutic INR
Historical Xa antidote andexanet: US sales ended December 2025; use local PCC-based reversal protocols

aortic-dissection.name: Aortic dissection
aortic-dissection.core: Sudden maximal chest or back pain with vascular or neurologic deficits suggests aortic dissection, even without widened mediastinum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long-standing hypertension → **medial degeneration** in older adults; bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation
Marfan/vascular Ehlers-Danlos, pregnancy, cocaine, aortic instrumentation or aneurysm

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Abrupt severe pain**, pulse/BP asymmetry, syncope, focal neurologic deficit
New aortic regurgitation murmur; limb ischemia or abdominal pain from branch-vessel malperfusion
Hypotension suggests rupture, tamponade, severe regurgitation, or coronary involvement

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intimal tear → blood separates medial layers, creating false lumen
Propagation compromises branch arteries or ruptures into pericardium/pleura

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable → **CTA chest/abdomen/pelvis**; unstable or unable to leave resuscitation → bedside TEE
Chest radiograph may show widened mediastinum but normal film does not exclude dissection
ECG/troponin may mimic MI; high suspicion requires aortic imaging before antithrombotics
Examine bilateral arm pressures, femoral pulses, neurologic status, renal function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV esmolol or labetalol** + opioid analgesia; target HR 60–80 and SBP <120 if perfusion maintained
Persistent hypertension after rate control → nicardipine or nitroprusside; avoid vasodilator before beta blockade
★ **Avoid anticoagulation and thrombolysis** when dissection suspected
Tamponade from dissection → immediate surgical team; routine pericardiocentesis can worsen hemorrhage

rows.label: Complications
items: Aortic rupture, hemothorax, tamponade, MI, stroke, paraplegia, mesenteric/renal ischemia
Late aneurysmal dilation or recurrent dissection despite initial successful treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Lifelong **BP control and surveillance CTA/MRA**; beta-blocker-based regimen
Avoid heavy isometric lifting; screen first-degree relatives for familial aortopathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute coronary syndrome: pressure-like pain, no pulse deficit; coexistence possible
PE: pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, right-heart strain
Esophageal rupture: vomiting followed by pain and subcutaneous emphysema

aortic-dissection.evidence: Not checked online; established aortic emergency principles.

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.scope: Acute appendicitis, clinical presentation, pediatric and pregnancy considerations, imaging (ultrasound, CT), surgical management
appendicitis.core: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, followed by anorexia and nausea, suggests appendiceal inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescents/young adults; luminal obstruction by lymphoid hyperplasia or fecalith
Older adults may have obstructing neoplasm; immunosuppression can blunt findings

rows.label: Clues
items: McBurney tenderness, guarding, fever; Rovsing, psoas, or obturator signs depend on position
★ **Diffuse peritonitis, toxicity, hypotension** → perforation/sepsis until proven otherwise
Young children: nonspecific symptoms and rapid progression; pregnancy: displaced appendix, less reliable examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal obstruction → distention, venous congestion, bacterial invasion → ischemia/perforation
Visceral midgut pain precedes focal parietal peritoneal irritation

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, urinalysis, **pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; pyuria does not exclude appendicitis
★ Stable nonpregnant adult → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** when diagnosis uncertain
★ Child/pregnancy → **ultrasound first**; nondiagnostic → MRI without gadolinium, or CT in nonpregnant child
Noncompressible enlarged appendix >6 mm with periappendiceal inflammation supports diagnosis
Clear peritonitis → surgical evaluation; do not delay necessary operation for repeated imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ NPO, **IV fluids, IV opioids, ceftriaxone + metronidazole**, surgical consultation; opioids do not obscure exam
Laparoscopic appendectomy definitive; do not withhold necessary surgery during pregnancy
Selected uncomplicated cases → antibiotics after shared decision; recurrence/failure higher, especially with appendicolith
Localized abscess/phlegmon in stable patient → antibiotics ± image-guided drainage; follow-up based on age/risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Perforation, abscess, peritonitis, sepsis, ileus
Postoperative wound infection, intra-abdominal collection, adhesional obstruction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, adnexal findings
Ovarian torsion: sudden unilateral pelvic pain; gastroenteritis: diarrhea prominent before diffuse cramping
Mesenteric adenitis: viral prodrome, normal appendix on imaging

appendicitis.evidence: Not checked online; established general-surgery evaluation and treatment principles.

ards.name: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
ards.scope: Berlin definition, PaO2/FiO2 ratio, noncardiogenic pulmonary edema (normal PCWP), increased capillary permeability, lung-protective ventilation (low tidal volume, PEEP), prone positioning
ards.core: Acute refractory hypoxemia and bilateral opacities after a major inflammatory insult, without hydrostatic edema explaining the respiratory failure.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sepsis, pneumonia, aspiration, major trauma, pancreatitis, near-drowning, massive transfusion
Toxic shock syndrome: renal/hepatic injury common, but **ARDS** carries the highest mortality

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid tachypnea, increased work of breathing, diffuse crackles; oxygen requirements escalate
Severe disease: cyanosis, exhaustion, altered mentation, hypotension, multiorgan dysfunction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ Diffuse alveolar-capillary injury → **increased permeability**, protein-rich edema, hyaline membranes
Surfactant loss and alveolar collapse → decreased compliance and intrapulmonary shunt

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Berlin: onset **within 1 week**, bilateral imaging opacities, respiratory failure not explained by cardiac overload
ABG and FiO2 quantify severity; classification requires PEEP or CPAP ≥5 cm H2O
Echocardiography if hydrostatic edema remains plausible; PCWP generally normal, but pulmonary artery catheter unnecessary

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat precipitating cause; oxygen → intubation for severe respiratory distress or refractory hypoxemia
★ Ventilate at **6 mL/kg predicted body weight**; plateau pressure ≤30 cm H2O
★ Moderate/severe → higher **PEEP**; PaO2/FiO2 <150 despite support → prone >12 hours/day
After shock resolves → conservative fluid strategy; avoid prolonged high-pressure recruitment maneuvers
Consider corticosteroids; early severe dyssynchrony → neuromuscular blockade; refractory severe disease → VV-ECMO evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Ventilator-induced lung injury, pneumothorax, ventilator-associated pneumonia
Critical illness weakness, delirium, persistent exercise limitation; mortality often reflects underlying multiorgan failure

rows.label: Prevention
items: Aspiration precautions, infection prevention, prompt sepsis treatment; avoid unnecessary transfusions
Daily sedation assessment, spontaneous breathing trials when improving, venous thromboembolism prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cardiogenic edema: elevated filling pressures, LV dysfunction, improvement with decongestion
Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage: falling hemoglobin; progressively bloodier bronchoalveolar lavage
Pulmonary embolism: hypoxemia with relatively clear imaging; CT pulmonary angiography identifies thrombus

attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.scope: Diagnostic criteria across two settings, behavioral rating scales from parents and teachers, behavioral therapy, stimulant pharmacotherapy
attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.core: Persistent developmentally inappropriate inattention and/or hyperactivity–impulsivity causing functional impairment across settings, with childhood onset.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong genetic contribution, prematurity, prenatal tobacco/alcohol exposure; symptoms may persist into adulthood
Learning disorders, anxiety, oppositional behavior, sleep problems and substance use commonly coexist

rows.label: Clues
items: Inattention: lost items, distraction, disorganization; hyperactivity: fidgeting, leaving seat, excessive talking
Impulsivity: interrupting, difficulty waiting; presentations can be inattentive, hyperactive–impulsive, or combined
Academic difficulty alone insufficient; assess family, peer, driving, and workplace function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Altered dopamine/norepinephrine executive-control signaling; inconsistent performance does not imply deliberate behavior

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥6 symptoms per domain**, or ≥5 if age ≥17; duration ≥6 months
★ Several symptoms **before age 12**, present in ≥2 settings, with impairment; exclude better explanations
Parent and teacher DSM-based rating scales, such as Vanderbilt; interview child and evaluate comorbidities
Check vision/hearing, sleep, learning needs; no routine EEG, neuroimaging, or laboratory diagnostic test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Ages 4–5: **parent-training behavioral management** first; methylphenidate for persistent moderate/severe impairment
★ Age ≥6: **methylphenidate or amphetamine** plus behavioral/classroom intervention and educational supports
Atomoxetine, extended-release guanfacine/clonidine when stimulants unsuitable, ineffective, or diversion concerning
Before prescribing: personal/family cardiac history, BP/HR, height/weight; ECG only if cardiac concern
Titrate to function and adverse effects; monitor appetite, sleep, growth, BP, misuse; reassess across settings

rows.label: Complications
items: Injury, academic failure, relationship problems; untreated impairment increases later substance-use risk
Stimulants → appetite suppression, insomnia, tachycardia; atomoxetine → suicidality warning, rare liver injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Routines, sleep, positive reinforcement, school accommodations; secure medication against diversion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Absence seizures: brief stereotyped unresponsiveness with abrupt recovery
Anxiety: attention disrupted by worry
Sleep apnea: snoring, poor sleep, daytime behavioral dysfunction

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess
**Cracked, excoriated nipples** → main portal of entry for lactational mastitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: cystic lactational/postlactational mass, no inflammation, varies with feeds; fat–fluid level on imaging
Mastitis: focal tender erythema, fever, no fluctuance; abscess adds **fluctuance**; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → usually **papilloma**; exclude malignancy, persistent → surgical evaluation
Nonbloody discharge only on expression, normal exam → **physiologic**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma
Cyclic bilateral nodularity, no dominant mass → **reexamine after menses**, before imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Painful simple cyst → aspiration; nonbloody fluid + full collapse → benign; bloody fluid/residual mass → **biopsy**
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Breast pain, no mass, young, normal exam → **reassurance**; fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID
★ Mastitis → **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**, keep breastfeeding/pumping; abscess → add needle/incision drainage; MRSA → clindamycin
Tender lactating lump, no erythema/fever → **warm compresses**, keep nursing; persistent galactocele → aspiration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

table.title: Common benign findings
rows: Early postpartum; bilateral tense tender breasts, low fever

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

benign-skin-growths.name: Benign skin growths
benign-skin-growths.scope: Seborrheic keratosis, dermatofibroma, acrochordon, lipoma, epidermoid cyst
benign-skin-growths.core: Slow-growing, stable superficial lesions usually need reassurance; morphology guides recognition, while atypical change requires tissue diagnosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging → keratoses; friction, obesity, insulin resistance → skin tags
Minor trauma may precede dermatofibroma; blocked follicular openings favor epidermoid cysts
Lipomas often sporadic or familial; multiple lesions do not automatically imply malignancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Most lesions asymptomatic; irritation, snagging, cosmetic concern may prompt consultation
★ **Rapid growth, ulceration, spontaneous bleeding**, fixation, or new irregular pigment → reassess diagnosis
Deep, painful, enlarging soft-tissue mass, especially >5 cm → evaluate for sarcoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Benign keratinocyte, fibrous, adipose, or follicular proliferation; no inherent need for oncologic excision
Ruptured keratin cyst → sterile inflammation; erythema alone does not prove bacterial infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical lesions → **clinical examination**; compare with surrounding skin and prior photographs
Uncertain pigmented lesion → dermoscopy and biopsy; do not destroy before excluding melanoma
Suspicious deep mass → MRI and specialist-directed biopsy; ultrasound can establish superficial cystic character

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Reassurance** for confidently benign, untroublesome lesions; treatment chosen for symptoms or cosmetic goals
Irritated keratosis/tag → cryotherapy, snip, or shave removal; dermatofibroma usually observed
Symptomatic lipoma → excision; large/deep or suspicious masses need evaluation before office removal
★ Epidermoid cyst → **complete capsule excision** after inflammation subsides; fluctuant abscess → incision/drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: Local irritation, secondary infection, cyst rupture; removal → bleeding, scar, recurrence
Premature reassurance of atypical growth can delay cancer diagnosis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Melanoma: evolving asymmetric pigmentation, irregular border, color variation
Squamous cell carcinoma: indurated, scaly or ulcerated enlarging lesion
Liposarcoma: deep progressive mass rather than small soft mobile nodule

table.title: Morphologic recognition
rows: Firm papule; dimples with lateral compression

benign-skin-growths.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatologic morphology and evaluation principles.

birth-trauma.name: Birth trauma
birth-trauma.scope: Caput succedaneum, cephalohematoma, subgaleal hemorrhage, clavicular fracture, facial nerve palsy (forceps compression), Erb-Duchenne palsy (C5-C6), Klumpke palsy (C8-T1), clinical course and management
birth-trauma.core: After difficult delivery, distinguish benign scalp swelling from occult hemorrhage and identify focal bone or peripheral nerve injuries.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Vacuum/forceps, shoulder dystocia, macrosomia, malpresentation, prolonged or precipitous delivery
Traction/compression can injure nerves; spontaneous delivery does not exclude neonatal trauma

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Increasing head circumference, pallor, tachycardia, poor perfusion** → concealed scalp hemorrhage until proven otherwise
Asymmetric Moro response → fracture or brachial plexus injury; inspect spontaneous movement and grasp
Clavicular crepitus/tenderness or later callus; pain-limited movement can mimic neurologic weakness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Scalp compartments differ in capacity and suture boundaries; broad potential spaces permit major blood loss
Peripheral compression causes neurapraxia; traction may produce more severe plexus disruption

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical scalp examination plus **serial head circumference and hematocrit** when bleeding suspected
Trend vitals/perfusion; CBC, coagulation studies, crossmatch for expanding swelling
Suspected fracture → clavicle radiograph if uncertain; assess joints and distinguish pain from paralysis
Facial injury: asymmetric cry and incomplete eyelid closure; examine forehead to localize peripheral palsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Shock/expanding subgaleal collection → **NICU, IV resuscitation and blood products** immediately
★ Cephalohematoma: observe bilirubin/hematocrit; **never aspirate routinely** because infection risk
Clavicular fracture → gentle handling, analgesia, brief immobilization; usually heals rapidly
Plexus injury → gentle range-of-motion/physical treatment, early follow-up; persistent deficits → specialist
Facial palsy → lubricate/protect incompletely closing eye; most compression injuries recover over weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Blood breakdown → jaundice; massive hemorrhage → anemia, DIC, shock
Severe plexus injury → contractures and persistent weakness; corneal injury with incomplete closure

rows.label: Prevention
items: Careful instrument selection/traction, shoulder-dystocia maneuvers and team training; postinstrument delivery surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Congenital muscular torticollis: sternocleidomastoid tightness rather than limb weakness
Central neurologic injury: seizures, altered alertness, broader motor abnormalities

table.title: Localization
rows: Subcutaneous edema; crosses sutures; resolves days
Subperiosteal blood; does not cross sutures; resolves weeks
Diffuse boggy expanding swelling; crosses sutures
Waiter's tip; absent Moro, preserved grasp
Weak hand/grasp; possible ipsilateral Horner syndrome

birth-trauma.evidence: Not checked online; established neonatal trauma recognition and stabilization teaching.

bladder-cancer.name: Bladder cancer
bladder-cancer.scope: Urothelial (transitional cell) carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, painless gross hematuria, smoking and occupational exposures, cystoscopy, transurethral resection
bladder-cancer.core: Painless gross hematuria in an older adult requires evaluation for urinary tract malignancy, even during anticoagulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Smoking**, aromatic amines in dye/rubber industries; older age and male sex
Cyclophosphamide, pelvic radiation; chronic catheter irritation and Schistosoma haematobium predispose to squamous carcinoma

rows.label: Clues
items: Intermittent bleeding, clots; carcinoma in situ may produce irritative voiding symptoms without a visible mass
Advanced disease: pelvic pain, hydronephrosis, weight loss, or bone pain

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Urothelial field injury → multifocal tumors and recurrence throughout the collecting system
Squamous metaplasia from chronic inflammation → keratinizing malignancy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Cystoscopy + CT urography** evaluate bladder and upper tracts; urinalysis/culture assess alternatives
Urine cytology helps detect high-grade disease/CIS; negative cytology does not exclude cancer
★ **TURBT including muscularis propria** establishes histology, grade, and depth
T1 disease → repeat resection within 6 weeks; invasive disease → chest/abdomen/pelvis staging

rows.label: Tx
items: Clot retention → large-bore catheter, irrigation; persistent obstruction or bleeding → urgent urology
Selected fit patients seeking bladder preservation → maximal resection plus concurrent chemoradiation
Avoid intravesical chemotherapy with suspected bladder perforation; BCG contraindicated during active symptomatic UTI

rows.label: Complications
items: Obstructive renal failure, recurrent hemorrhage, nodal or distant metastases
Intravesical BCG → cystitis; rarely disseminated infection; cystectomy → diversion-related metabolic complications

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation and occupational protection; no routine population screening
★ **Surveillance cystoscopy** after treatment because recurrence is common; interval based on risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nephrolithiasis: colicky flank pain, stone on noncontrast CT
Glomerulonephritis: dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts, proteinuria
Cystitis: dysuria and positive culture; persistent hematuria after treatment still needs evaluation
Urethral carcinoma: older woman, blood spotting, friable urethral meatal mass, irritative/obstructive voiding

table.title: Depth determines definitive treatment
rows: TURBT + intravesical BCG; selected early cystectomy

bone-tumors.name: Bone tumors
bone-tumors.scope: Osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, chondrosarcoma, giant cell tumor of bone, osteochondroma, osteoid osteoma, bone metastases, biopsy
bone-tumors.core: Persistent focal bone pain, a growing mass, or a destructive radiographic lesion requires planned evaluation before biopsy or fixation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Osteosarcoma: adolescence, hereditary retinoblastoma (RB1), prior radiation, Paget disease; chondrosarcoma: older adults
Hereditary multiple exostoses predispose to osteochondromas; most adult malignant bone lesions are metastases

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Night/rest pain**, enlarging mass, constitutional symptoms or pathologic fracture → concerning lesion
Osteoid osteoma: nocturnal pain relieved by NSAIDs; small cortical nidus
Osteochondroma: painless metaphyseal exostosis with medullary continuity; new growth after maturity concerning
Known cancer + constant back pain, vertebral point tenderness → **spinal metastasis**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tumor lineage determines osteoid, cartilage or primitive-cell production; aggressive growth destroys cortex
Giant cell tumor: neoplastic stromal cells recruit osteoclast-like giant cells, causing locally aggressive osteolysis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Plain radiographs first**; assess location, margins, periosteal reaction and matrix
Aggressive lesion → MRI entire involved bone/adjacent joint; chest CT for lung metastases
★ **Orthopedic oncology plans biopsy tract**; core biopsy after imaging, before definitive treatment
CBC, ESR/CRP if infection suspected; normal labs do not exclude malignancy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Osteosarcoma → **neoadjuvant chemotherapy + wide resection**, then postoperative chemotherapy
Ewing → systemic chemotherapy plus surgery and/or radiation
Chondrosarcoma → wide surgical excision; conventional tumors relatively chemo/radioresistant
Symptomatic osteoid osteoma → radiofrequency ablation; asymptomatic osteochondroma → observation
Giant cell tumor → curettage/reconstruction; selected unresectable lesions → denosumab

rows.label: Complications
items: Pathologic fracture, neurovascular compromise, pulmonary metastases; limb surgery and chemotherapy morbidity
Mandible metastasis → mental nerve anesthesia (**numb chin**)

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: infection markers, cultures; may closely resemble Ewing
Bone metastases: older adult, multiple lesions; myeloma: anemia, monoclonal protein
Unicameral bone cyst: child, lucent expansile proximal humerus lesion; pathologic fracture after minor trauma

bone-tumors.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

brain-death.name: Brain death
brain-death.scope: Prerequisites (normothermia, normal BP), clinical exam (coma, absent brainstem reflexes), apnea test, ancillary testing (cerebral blood flow studies)
brain-death.core: Permanent loss of all brain function, including brainstem function, constitutes death; a beating heart on ventilation does not negate the diagnosis.

rows.label: Principle
items: Known catastrophic irreversible brain injury; compatible neuroimaging; adequate observation period
No family consent needed; after declaration → stop ventilator, unless organ donation planned

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Prerequisites: **temperature ≥36°C**, adult SBP ≥100 and MAP ≥75 mm Hg
Exclude paralysis/metabolic confounders; sedatives: ≥5 half-lives, longer if impaired clearance
★ Examination: **coma**, no brain-mediated motor response; absent brainstem reflexes (table)

rows.label: Don't
items: Oculocephalic testing with possible cervical injury; use caloric testing after confirming ear integrity
Declare death with any brain-mediated response or spontaneous breath
Use ancillary testing to bypass hypothermia or high CNS-depressant levels

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Spinal reflex movements may persist without contradicting diagnosis
Incomplete examination or unsafe apnea test → radionuclide cerebral perfusion or catheter angiography
After temperature ≤35.5°C, wait ≥24 hours following rewarming to ≥36°C

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Apnea test: no breaths, **PaCO2 ≥60 and ≥20 above baseline**, pH <7.30
Preoxygenate; abort apnea testing for hypotension, hypoxemia or unstable arrhythmia
★ 2023 update: **EEG no longer accepted** as ancillary testing; pediatric requirements differ

breast-cancer-screening.name: Breast cancer screening
breast-cancer-screening.scope: USPSTF screening mammography recommendations, age-based intervals, high-risk screening (BRCA, prior chest radiation, breast MRI), clinical breast exam, diagnostic evaluation of abnormal screening
breast-cancer-screening.core: USPSTF recommends biennial mammography from ages 40–74 for average-risk women; symptoms require diagnostic evaluation regardless of screening schedule.

rows.label: Who
items: Average risk includes family history or dense breasts without a defined high-risk syndrome
★ BRCA pathogenic variant, young chest irradiation or lifetime risk **≥20–25%** → high-risk pathway

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Age ≥75: insufficient USPSTF evidence; individualize by health, life expectancy and preference
High risk: annual MRI plus mammography, typically around age 30; specialist-tailored earlier MRI
BRCA1/2: **bilateral mastectomy + salpingo-oophorectomy** = greatest risk reduction; tamoxifen weaker

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Digital mammography/tomosynthesis; **MRI supplements**, not replaces, high-risk mammography
Clinical breast examination and breast self-examination do not substitute for imaging

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ BI-RADS 0 → **diagnostic views/targeted ultrasound**; 4–5 → core needle biopsy
BI-RADS 3 → short-interval imaging, usually 6 months; 1–2 → routine interval
Palpable concerning mass with negative imaging → tissue assessment for clinical–radiologic discordance

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Older teaching: 50; **2024 USPSTF starts at 40**; other societies accept annual
Dense breasts alone: insufficient USPSTF evidence for routine supplemental ultrasound/MRI
Harms: false positives, biopsy, overdiagnosis; concerning mass needs evaluation despite normal mammogram

breast-neoplasia.name: Breast neoplasia
breast-neoplasia.scope: Ductal carcinoma in situ, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), metastatic disease (bone, visceral), surgical management, endocrine and chemotherapy
breast-neoplasia.core: A suspicious breast lesion requires core biopsy, assessment of invasion and ER/PR/HER2 status to guide local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, BRCA-related syndromes, close-relative family history (distant relative adds little), prior chest irradiation
**Combined estrogen-progestin therapy**, prolonged estrogen, postmenopausal obesity, alcohol; atypical proliferative lesions

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless hard irregular mass, skin/nipple retraction, unilateral bloody discharge or axillary node
★ Peau d’orange, diffuse erythema and edema → **inflammatory breast cancer**, even without discrete mass
Persistent unilateral eczematous nipple lesion → Paget disease; **full-thickness biopsy**, investigate underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Invasion through basement membrane enables lymphatic/hematogenous metastasis
ER/PR signaling and HER2 amplification create actionable tumor drivers; triple-negative tumors lack these targets

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diagnostic mammography + targeted ultrasound** → core biopsy of suspicious lesion; pregnancy → **ultrasound first**
Pathology: invasion, grade, **ER/PR/HER2**; assess regional nodes clinically and with targeted imaging
Clinically node-negative invasive disease, including microinvasion ≤1 mm → sentinel node biopsy during definitive surgery
Distant staging scans for advanced disease or suspicious symptoms; not every small asymptomatic cancer
Axillary node adenocarcinoma, normal mammogram → occult breast primary; breast MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early: lumpectomy + radiation or mastectomy; **positive margins → reexcision** before adjuvant therapy
ER-positive → tamoxifen or postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor; chemotherapy based on stage/biology
★ HER2-positive → **trastuzumab-based** treatment, monitor LVEF; triple-negative → chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab if higher-risk
Locally advanced → neoadjuvant treatment, then surgery/radiation; large residual + palpable nodes → **mastectomy + axillary dissection**
Bone metastases → **zoledronate/denosumab**; systemic treatment by receptors, chemotherapy for visceral crisis

rows.label: Complications
items: Metastases to bone (often **mixed lytic–blastic**), lung, liver, brain; surgery/radiation → lymphedema
Tamoxifen → VTE/endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors → bone loss; trastuzumab → cardiomyopathy
Prior cancer + severe hypercalcemia, lytic lesions → recurrence; thiazide/calcium supplements cause only mild elevation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Age/risk-based screening, genetic counseling for suggestive pedigree; selected high-risk patients → chemoprevention
BRCA-related very high risk → discuss risk-reducing surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mastitis: lactation-associated tenderness/fever, improves with antibiotics
Fat necrosis: trauma/surgery history; biopsy if discordant imaging

table.title: Histologic distinctions
rows: Bilateral risk marker; discohesive lobular cells
Surveillance/risk reduction if concordant; later cancer usually ductal

breast-neoplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established breast-oncology management principles.

bronchiectasis.name: Bronchiectasis
bronchiectasis.scope: Cystic fibrosis, post-infectious, high-resolution CT, airway clearance, pseudomonas colonization, acute exacerbation
bronchiectasis.core: Chronic productive cough with recurrent respiratory infections and permanently dilated bronchi on high-resolution CT.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cystic fibrosis, prior severe pneumonia/TB, primary ciliary dyskinesia, aspiration, immunodeficiency
ABPA, rheumatoid arthritis, obstructing endobronchial lesion; some cases remain idiopathic

rows.label: Clues
items: Copious purulent sputum, coarse crackles, recurrent focal infections, hemoptysis, sometimes clubbing
Exacerbation: increased sputum volume/purulence, cough, dyspnea, fatigue; hypoxemia or sepsis → severe disease
Early lifelong infections, sinusitis, infertility, or situs inversus suggest impaired ciliary clearance
Child: chronic cough refractory to bronchodilators, steroids, antibiotics + persistent focal collapse/consolidation → localized bronchiectasis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired mucus clearance → persistent infection and neutrophilic inflammation → irreversible airway wall destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **High-resolution chest CT**: signet-ring bronchi, absent tapering, airways visible near pleura, cystic spaces ± air-fluid levels
Sputum bacterial and mycobacterial cultures; spirometry measures associated airflow limitation
Quantitative immunoglobulins; total IgE/Aspergillus testing for ABPA; sweat chloride if CF suspected
Localized disease → bronchoscopy for tumor/foreign body; diffuse disease → investigate systemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daily **airway clearance**, exercise; bronchodilator for obstruction; no routine inhaled steroids or non-CF dornase alfa
★ Exacerbation → sputum culture then antibiotics guided by prior isolates; often **14 days**
Pseudomonas susceptible → ciprofloxacin; severe infection → IV cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam
★ ≥2 yearly or ≥1 severe exacerbation → azithromycin after NTM exclusion; chronic Pseudomonas → inhaled tobramycin
Massive hemoptysis → airway protection and bronchial artery embolization; focal refractory disease → resection evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic Pseudomonas colonization, resistant infection, respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension
Antibiotic toxicity/resistance; macrolides can cause QT prolongation and hearing impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, aspiration management, treatment of underlying immunodeficiency
New Pseudomonas isolation → specialist eradication regimen, often ciprofloxacin followed by inhaled antibiotic

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chronic bronchitis: smoking-related sputum without characteristic bronchial dilation
Lung abscess: solitary cavity with air-fluid level; no lifelong productive cough
Pulmonary TB: constitutional illness and compatible imaging; mycobacterial testing confirms

candidiasis.name: Candidiasis
candidiasis.scope: Oropharyngeal candidiasis (thrush), diaper candidiasis, intertrigo, vulvovaginal candidiasis, cell-mediated vs neutrophil immunity, nystatin, fluconazole
candidiasis.core: Opportunistic yeast overgrowth on mucosa or moist skin; distribution and host immune defects determine evaluation and antifungal route.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent antibiotics, diabetes, pregnancy, inhaled/systemic steroids, HIV; infants, dentures, skin occlusion
Neutropenia, central venous catheters, parenteral nutrition → invasive infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Odynophagia or dysphagia with immunosuppression** → esophageal involvement, even without visible oral lesions
Persistent/recurrent thrush outside infancy → evaluate HIV, diabetes, or other immune defects
Sepsis in neutropenic or catheterized host → consider candidemia rather than isolated superficial disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **T-cell/IL-17 dysfunction → mucocutaneous disease; neutrophil defects → invasive candidiasis**
Candida albicans: budding yeast and pseudohyphae; overgrowth of endogenous flora rather than routine sexual transmission

rows.label: Dx
items: Typical oral/cutaneous disease → clinical diagnosis; uncertain lesions → KOH microscopy
★ Vaginal symptoms → wet mount/KOH; **pH usually <4.5**; negative microscopy with suspicion → culture
Complicated/recurrent vaginitis → culture/speciation; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: Esophageal disease → **systemic fluconazole 14–21 days**; refractory symptoms → endoscopy with biopsy
★ Pregnancy → **7-day intravaginal clotrimazole**; systemic triazoles contraindicated
Recurrent vaginitis ≥3 episodes/year → extended induction then weekly fluconazole for 6 months
Candidemia → IV micafungin and blood cultures; investigate/remove infected catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Poor oral intake, painful fissures, recurrent vaginitis; invasive disease → endophthalmitis, endocarditis, organ abscesses
Azoles: hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation, CYP interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rinse mouth after inhaled steroids; clean dentures, keep folds dry, change wet diapers promptly
Optimize glucose control and HIV ART; routine partner treatment unnecessary for uncomplicated vaginitis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Leukoplakia/oral hairy leukoplakia: white plaques do not scrape off
Irritant diaper dermatitis: spares folds; bacterial vaginosis: fishy odor, elevated vaginal pH

table.title: Superficial presentations
rows: Beefy erythema, satellite pustules; folds involved
Topical azole or single-dose oral fluconazole

carcinoid-syndrome.name: Carcinoid syndrome
carcinoid-syndrome.scope: Neuroendocrine tumors (midgut, bronchial), episodic cutaneous flushing, secretory diarrhea, tricuspid and pulmonary valvular disease, 24-hour urine 5-HIAA, octreotide therapy, surgical resection
carcinoid-syndrome.core: Episodic flushing and secretory diarrhea in a patient with a neuroendocrine tumor, often with liver metastases.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Midgut NET, especially ileal; bronchial NET with systemic venous drainage

rows.label: Clues
items: Watery stools persist during fasting; episodic wheezing
★ Right-sided valve disease: **tricuspid regurgitation** and pulmonic stenosis; edema, JVD
Left-sided valve disease possible with bronchial NET or right-to-left intracardiac shunt
Carcinoid crisis: abrupt hypotension or hypertension, bronchospasm and hemodynamic instability

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hepatic metabolism normally clears portal vasoactive products; hepatic metastases or systemic drainage bypass first pass
Serotonin drives diarrhea and endocardial fibrosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **24-hour urine 5-HIAA**; avoid serotonin-rich foods and interfering drugs before collection
CT/MRI and somatostatin receptor PET for localization and staging; tissue grading guides tumor therapy
NT-proBNP >260 pg/mL or cardiac signs → echocardiogram

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Octreotide** or lanreotide for hormonal symptoms and tumor control
Resect localized disease; selected metastatic cases → hepatic debulking or liver-directed therapy
Refractory diarrhea despite somatostatin analog → add telotristat
★ Carcinoid crisis → IV octreotide, fluids, vasopressors

rows.label: Complications
items: Right heart failure; mesenteric fibrosis → obstruction or ischemia
Tryptophan diversion → niacin deficiency and pellagra

rows.label: Prevention
items: Periprocedural planning for crisis risk during anesthesia or tumor manipulation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pheochromocytoma: episodic hypertension, headache, diaphoresis
VIPoma: profound watery diarrhea, hypokalemia, achlorhydria

carcinoid-syndrome.evidence: Checked ENETS guidance on carcinoid syndrome and carcinoid heart disease (2022).

cardiomyopathies.name: Cardiomyopathies
cardiomyopathies.scope: Dilated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, restrictive cardiomyopathy, stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy, viral myocarditis, diagnostic evaluation, management
cardiomyopathies.core: Myocardial disease causes pump failure, impaired filling, dynamic obstruction, or arrhythmias; echocardiography defines the phenotype.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dilated: familial disease, alcohol, anthracyclines, peripartum state, **viral myocarditis**
Hypertrophic: autosomal dominant sarcomeric variants; restrictive: amyloid, hemochromatosis, radiation
Takotsubo: emotional/physical stress; myocarditis: recent viral illness, immune checkpoint inhibitors

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, edema, elevated JVP; **displaced PMI**, S3 → dilated LV; syncope/ventricular arrhythmia signals danger
★ Obstructive HCM murmur **↑Valsalva/standing**, ↓squatting/handgrip; exertional presyncope
Myocarditis: chest discomfort, tachycardia disproportionate to fever, acute heart failure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sarcomere dysfunction or myocardial injury → remodeling; infiltration → reduced ventricular compliance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG, troponin, BNP → transthoracic echo**; assess coronary ischemia when suspected
Cardiac MRI: inflammation, scar, infiltrative patterns; iron studies or monoclonal protein testing when relevant
Endomyocardial biopsy: selected fulminant unexplained failure, malignant arrhythmias, suspected giant-cell myocarditis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ HFrEF: **ARNI, evidence-based beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor**; loop diuretic for congestion
Obstructive HCM: nonvasodilating beta-blocker (propranolol, metoprolol); alternative verapamil/diltiazem
Refractory obstruction → myosin inhibitor, disopyramide, or septal reduction; avoid dehydration and vasodilators
Restrictive disease: cautious diuresis, treat cause; Takotsubo: supportive care after excluding ACS
Myocarditis with shock → ICU, circulatory support; no routine antiviral or immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Sudden cardiac death, atrial fibrillation, thromboembolism; advanced failure → transplantation evaluation
★ HCM with cardiac arrest or major sudden-death risk → **ICD** consideration

rows.label: Prevention
items: Screen first-degree relatives in inherited disease; avoid cardiotoxins
Myocarditis: restrict strenuous exercise until clinical recovery and reassessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic cardiomyopathy: obstructive coronary disease explains dysfunction
Constrictive pericarditis: pericardial disease, respiratory ventricular interdependence
Aortic stenosis: murmur softer with standing/Valsalva, unlike obstructive HCM

table.title: Echo phenotype
rows: Enlarged ventricles, diffuse hypokinesia, reduced EF
Transient apical ballooning beyond coronary territory

cardiomyopathies.evidence: HCM checked 2026-10-30: [AHA/ACC 2024](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/05/06/15/12/2024-hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy-gl); other content established teaching.

carotid-artery-stenosis.name: Carotid artery stenosis
carotid-artery-stenosis.scope: Asymptomatic carotid bruit, carotid duplex ultrasound, medical management, indications for carotid endarterectomy
carotid-artery-stenosis.core: Carotid atherosclerosis causes ipsilateral retinal or cerebral ischemia; intervention depends on symptoms, stenosis severity, and operative risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia; coronary or peripheral arterial disease
Prior neck radiation increases stenosis and surgical complexity

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Amaurosis fugax** (painless curtain-like monocular vision loss), contralateral weakness, aphasia → symptomatic disease
Bruit may be incidental; loudness does not measure severity, complete occlusion may be silent
Isolated dizziness or syncope rarely represents carotid-territory ischemia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Plaque rupture → artery-to-artery emboli; critical narrowing can reduce cerebral perfusion
Retinal **Hollenhorst plaque** (cholesterol embolus) → ulcerated ipsilateral carotid plaque

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected stenosis or selected incidental bruit evaluation → **carotid duplex ultrasound**
CTA/MRA confirms anatomy before intervention; brain imaging evaluates neurologic deficits
★ **No routine screening** of asymptomatic general adults; bruit auscultation is an unreliable screen

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ All: **antiplatelet + high-intensity statin**, BP and diabetes control
Symptomatic operative candidates: endarterectomy generally within **2 weeks**, after neurologic stabilization
Classic asymptomatic CEA criteria: ≥70%, life expectancy ≥3–5 years, perioperative stroke/death <3%; individualized decision
CREST-2: asymptomatic stenting benefited selected patients; CEA lacked significant benefit; avoid automatic surgery
Symptomatic older adults: CEA generally preferred to stenting; high surgical-risk anatomy may favor stenting

rows.label: Complications
items: Ischemic stroke, recurrent TIAs; procedure → stroke, MI, cranial nerve injury
Hyperperfusion after revascularization → headache, seizures, brain hemorrhage; driven by **postoperative hypertension**
New deficit after endarterectomy → **noncontrast head CT** first: hemorrhage vs carotid thrombosis; no heparin/tPA beforehand
★ Expanding neck hematoma with stridor → **open wound/emergent neck exploration**; no imaging delay

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, exercise, Mediterranean-style diet; sustained vascular risk reduction
New focal neurologic symptoms → emergency stroke assessment, even after symptom resolution

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic stenosis: cardiac murmur radiates to both carotids
Cardioembolism: atrial fibrillation or cardiac thrombus; multiple vascular territories
Migraine aura: gradually spreading positive visual/sensory symptoms
Giant cell arteritis: headache, jaw claudication, ↑ESR; vision loss often persistent

table.title: Symptomatic ipsilateral stenosis
rows: Selected patients: age, sex, comorbidity matter

cervical-artery-dissection.name: Cervical artery dissection
cervical-artery-dissection.scope: Carotid artery dissection, vertebral artery dissection, Horner syndrome, posterior circulation stroke, imaging, antithrombotic therapy
cervical-artery-dissection.core: Young or middle-aged adult with sudden unilateral head or neck pain followed by retinal or cerebral ischemia after minor neck trauma.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Neck manipulation, hyperextension, sporting injury, coughing; spontaneous cases common
Fibromuscular dysplasia, connective-tissue disorders, migraine, recent infection

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Painful partial Horner syndrome**: ptosis + miosis, often without facial anhidrosis
Carotid: monocular visual loss, aphasia, contralateral weakness; pulsatile tinnitus possible
Vertebral: occipital pain, ataxia, vertigo; **lateral medullary syndrome** (crossed sensory loss, hoarseness, Horner)
Pain may precede ischemia by hours or days; normal initial neurologic examination does not exclude dissection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intimal tear or vasa vasorum hemorrhage → intramural hematoma and arterial narrowing
Mural thrombus embolization usually causes stroke; expansion may compress adjacent sympathetic fibers

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CTA head and neck** rapidly evaluates carotid/vertebral lumen and associated occlusion
MRA with fat-suppressed neck MRI identifies mural hematoma; brain MRI detects infarction
Tapered stenosis, intimal flap, pseudoaneurysm support diagnosis; catheter angiography for equivocal/interventional cases
Do not rely on carotid ultrasound alone for distal carotid or vertebral lesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Eligible acute ischemic stroke → **IV thrombolysis and/or thrombectomy**; dissection alone is no exclusion
★ Extracranial dissection → **antiplatelet or anticoagulation for 3–6 months**, individualized bleeding/ischemic risk
Repeat vascular imaging guides follow-up; no proven universal superiority of anticoagulation
Recurrent ischemia despite medical treatment or critical hemodynamic compromise → specialist consideration of stenting
Intracranial extension/subarachnoid hemorrhage → urgent neurovascular consultation; avoid reflex anticoagulation

rows.label: Complications
items: TIA, retinal infarction, ischemic stroke, dissecting pseudoaneurysm
Intracranial dissections may rupture into subarachnoid space; recurrent extracranial events uncommon

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid neck manipulation/contact injury while healing; control vascular risks
High-risk connective-tissue disease → individualized long-term activity counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cluster headache: episodic autonomic headache without persistent ischemic findings
Pancoast tumor: gradual Horner syndrome with shoulder/arm symptoms
BPPV: brief positional vertigo without focal deficits or acute neck pain

child-abuse-and-neglect.name: Child abuse and neglect
child-abuse-and-neglect.scope: Physical abuse (burn patterns, fractures of different ages, metaphyseal corner fractures), abusive head trauma (shaken baby, subdural hematoma, retinal hemorrhages), neglect, mandatory reporting
child-abuse-and-neglect.core: Reasonable suspicion of child maltreatment requires protective reporting; proof and caregiver permission are unnecessary.

rows.label: Principle
items: Inconsistent history, delayed care, or developmentally impossible mechanism increase suspicion

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Report to child protective services** promptly; urgent danger → emergency protective services
