★ Functional deficit or negative workups → **psychiatric assessment**, no more procedures; **new red flags → reassess**
Factitious: team approach, factual records, no confrontation, evaluate psychiatric comorbidity; protect dependents from induced illness

rows.label: Complications
items: Iatrogenic injury, unnecessary surgery, opioid exposure, disability, fragmented care
Factitious disorder imposed on another → serious abuse risk requiring safeguarding action

rows.label: Mimics
items: Occult medical disease: evolving objective findings or coherent physiologic abnormalities
Delusional disorder: fixed somatic belief despite evidence, without flexible doubt

table.title: Distinguishing patterns
rows: Motor/sensory symptoms incompatible with neurologic disease
Intentional deception; no obvious external reward
Intentional symptoms, external gain; no treatment/invasive testing

somatic-symptom-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established DSM-5-TR teaching.

study-designs.name: Study designs
study-designs.scope: Case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, RCT, control selection, bias, internal and external validity
study-designs.core: Study design determines how participants are selected, when exposure/outcome are measured, and which associations can be estimated without avoidable bias.

rows.label: Definition
items: Internal validity: credible within-study inference; external validity: applicability elsewhere
**Selection/ascertainment bias**: institutional or already-ill sample misrepresents target population
Subjective scoring by different raters → **interobserver variability**; standardize criteria

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Randomization balances confounders on average**; concealed allocation prevents enrollment bias
Blinding reduces behavior/assessment bias; intention-to-treat retains original randomized groups
Loss to follow-up can bias estimates when related to exposure and outcome

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Case-control controls → **same source population** that produced cases, independent of exposure
Prospective measurement improves temporality but does not eliminate confounding in observational research
Life table: poorest 1-year survival → steepest interval drop, not lowest cumulative point

rows.label: Compare
items: Confounding: third-variable distortion; randomize, restrict, match, stratify, or adjust
Effect modification: association differs across strata; report rather than remove it
Clinician-chosen treatment → **selection bias/confounding by indication**; randomization prevents it

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case-control sampling cannot directly estimate incidence or risk** without additional population data
★ Cross-sectional data lack reliable **temporal sequence**; prevalent cases favor longer survivors
Random selection supports generalizability; random assignment supports causal inference

study-designs.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

substance-use-disorders.name: Substance use disorders
substance-use-disorders.scope: Diagnostic criteria (mild, moderate, severe), cocaine use disorder, amphetamine use disorder, cannabis use disorder, motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral therapy, 12-step programs
substance-use-disorders.core: A problematic pattern causing impaired control, risky use, social impairment or physiologic adaptation defines substance use disorder; severity follows criterion count.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, trauma, psychiatric comorbidity, early exposure, unstable housing and peer availability
Persistent psychosocial stress and limited treatment access worsen trajectory

rows.label: Clues
items: Tolerance/withdrawal not required; physiologic adaptation during prescribed use alone does not establish disorder
Stimulant withdrawal: fatigue, hypersomnia, depression and craving; assess suicide risk
Cannabis withdrawal: irritability, anxiety, insomnia and reduced appetite after sustained use
Caffeine withdrawal: diffuse headache 12–48 h after stopping intake, including NPO surgery; normal neurologic exam

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reward learning and neuroadaptation strengthen cue-driven behavior while impairing control
Cocaine blocks monoamine reuptake; amphetamines increase release; cannabinoids act mainly at CB1 receptors
THC lipophilic, adipose-stored: urine positive for weeks in chronic use; other drugs clear in days

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥2 of 11 DSM-5 criteria in 12 months**; severity **mild 2–3, moderate 4–5, severe ≥6**
Control/social: larger/longer use, failed cutdown, time spent, craving, role failure, social problems, abandoned activities
Risk/pharmacologic: hazardous use, continued despite physical/psychological harm, tolerance, withdrawal
Clinical interview establishes disorder; urine drug testing documents exposure, not severity or current impairment
Screen co-occurring depression, psychosis, HIV/hepatitis risk and polysubstance use; confirm unexpected immunoassay positives

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Motivational interviewing**: explore ambivalence, elicit personal goals, support autonomy; avoid confrontation
★ Stimulant disorder → **contingency management**, CBT/community reinforcement; no FDA-approved maintenance drug
Cannabis disorder → motivational enhancement, CBT and contingency management; no established approved medication
Peer/12-step programs as adjuncts; tailor outpatient versus residential intensity to safety/support and impairment
Stimulant agitation → benzodiazepines/cooling; uncomplicated cannabis intoxication, mild paranoia → observe, no drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Cocaine/amphetamine → MI, stroke, arrhythmia, psychosis; chronic methamphetamine → cardiomyopathy and dental injury
Cannabis → impaired driving, hyperemesis (cessation, fluids, capsaicin/haloperidol), anxiety or psychosis
Stimulant crash can precipitate severe depression/suicidality; withdrawal usually lacks alcohol-like autonomic danger
Older adults: new benzodiazepine (temazepam) → subacute ataxia, dysarthria, confusion, falls

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Harm reduction: **naloxone** for possible opioid contamination, avoid using alone, offer fentanyl testing access
Treat comorbid illness, relapse planning, overdose education and regular follow-up; recurrence prompts reassessment
Adolescent experimentation without impairment → counsel teen and family; no formal treatment program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bipolar mania: episodes persist independently of intoxication
Primary psychosis: symptoms outside substance exposure periods
ADHD: longstanding childhood-onset pattern, not episodic intoxication

substance-use-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ASAM/AAAP stimulant guideline 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11105801/); DSM-5 criteria established definitions.

table.title: Intoxication by substance
rows: Mydriasis, hypertension, hyperreflexia, paranoia, pressured speech
Violent agitation, hyperthermia; formication with excoriations; MDMA empathic
Red conjunctivae, dry mouth, tachycardia, hunger, slowed time
**Nystagmus**, analgesia, hypertension, myoclonus; violent-catatonic fluctuation, mutism
Perioral/perinasal rash, solvent odor, ataxia/slurring; clears <1 hour
Coma, apnea, hypotension, bradycardia, sluggish pupils

supraventricular-tachycardia.name: Supraventricular tachycardia
supraventricular-tachycardia.scope: AVNRT, AVRT, focal atrial tachycardia, vagal maneuvers, adenosine, synchronized cardioversion, catheter ablation
supraventricular-tachycardia.core: Abrupt rapid regular palpitations with a usually narrow QRS often represent AV-node-dependent reentry; stability determines immediate electrical versus pharmacologic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Accessory pathway, prior episodes, adrenergic triggers, caffeine/stimulants
Focal atrial tachycardia may accompany structural disease; incessant forms can cause cardiomyopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: Regular rate often 150–250/min; palpitations, lightheadedness, dyspnea, neck pounding
★ **Hypotension, shock, ischemic chest pain, altered mentation**, or acute HF → unstable tachycardia
WPW between episodes: short PR, delta wave, widened QRS; may be absent with concealed pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reentry requires distinct conduction/refractory properties; AV node participates in AVNRT and orthodromic AVRT
Adenosine transiently blocks AV conduction; automatic atrial rhythms may continue despite transient ventricular slowing

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **12-lead ECG during episode**, continuous rhythm monitoring; check electrolytes, medication/exposure triggers
Wide-complex rhythm uncertain → presume VT rather than casually applying narrow-complex algorithm
Structural concern → echocardiography; recurrent undocumented events → ambulatory monitoring/electrophysiology evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable with pulse → **synchronized cardioversion**; sedation if feasible without delaying rescue
★ Stable regular narrow rhythm → **modified Valsalva → rapid IV adenosine**
Persistent stable SVT → IV diltiazem/verapamil or beta blocker if no contraindication; cardioversion if unsuccessful
★ Irregular wide preexcited AF → **procainamide or cardioversion**; avoid AV-nodal blockers, including adenosine
Recurrent symptomatic AVNRT/AVRT or focal tachycardia → catheter ablation; selected patients use oral nodal blockers

rows.label: Complications
items: Syncope, demand ischemia, tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy; preexcited AF can degenerate to VF
Adenosine: brief flushing/chest pressure, bronchospasm; avoid in active severe bronchospasm

rows.label: Prevention
items: Teach vagal maneuver, limit personal triggers; discuss definitive ablation for recurrence
Ablation near AV node carries small heart-block risk; shared procedural decision

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sinus tachycardia: gradual rate changes, beat-to-beat variability, physiologic driver; infants rarely >220/min
Atrial flutter: atrial sawtooth waves, often ventricular rate near 150

supraventricular-tachycardia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AHA adult advanced life support](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-advanced-life-support), [ACC/AHA AF guideline (2023)](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2023.08.017).

syphilis.name: Syphilis
syphilis.scope: Primary syphilis, secondary syphilis, latent syphilis, tertiary syphilis, neurosyphilis, serologic testing, Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, penicillin therapy
syphilis.core: Treponema pallidum infection progresses through mucocutaneous, asymptomatic, and destructive stages; neurologic, ocular, or auditory disease can occur anytime.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Unprotected sex, multiple partners, HIV; transplacental transmission during pregnancy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Primary: **painless chancre** with regional lymphadenopathy
Secondary: palms/soles rash, condylomata lata, generalized nodes, patchy alopecia
Tertiary: gummas, ascending aortic aneurysm; tabes dorsalis, **Argyll Robertson pupils**, Charcot joint, or dementia
Latent: reactive serology without symptoms; early = acquired within 1 year

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Spirochete dissemination → endarteritis, young-adult meningovascular stroke; posterior column injury → sensory ataxia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RPR/VDRL + treponemal assay**; discordant reverse screen → second treponemal assay
Early chancre with negative serology → lesion testing or repeat serology
★ Neurologic deficits → **LP**; CSF-VDRL specific, negative result does not exclude
Quantitative RPR: early disease follow-up at 6/12 months; latent at 6/12/24 months
Tertiary disease → CSF assessment before treatment; isolated ocular/otic disease may not require LP

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pregnancy with penicillin allergy → **desensitization**, then stage-specific penicillin
Nonpregnant penicillin allergy, uncomplicated early infection → doxycycline for 14 days

rows.label: Complications
items: Jarisch-Herxheimer: fever/myalgias within 24 hours after treatment; supportive care, not allergy
Congenital infection → stillbirth, hearing loss, dental/bone abnormalities

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Partners exposed within **90 days** → presumptive early-syphilis treatment despite negative tests
Condoms; HIV testing; prenatal screening; serial RPR after treatment, fourfold rise suggests reinfection/failure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chancroid: painful ulcer, tender suppurative nodes
HSV: painful grouped vesicles; pityriasis rosea: herald patch, usually spares palms
Autoimmune false-positive RPR: negative confirmatory treponemal assay

syphilis.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [CDC STI guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/syphilis.htm), including linked stage-specific guidance.

teratogens.name: Teratogens
teratogens.scope: Valproate and carbamazepine (neural tube defects), ACE inhibitors, isotretinoin, lithium (Ebstein anomaly), warfarin, alcohol (fetal alcohol syndrome), high-dose folic acid supplementation
teratogens.core: Exposure timing and agent determine fetal harm; review medications before conception and substitute safer treatments while preserving maternal disease control.

rows.label: Use
items: Preconception counseling, exposure assessment, and selection of pregnancy-compatible drugs
Inadvertent early oral contraceptive exposure → not teratogenic; reassure, no invasive testing
Live vaccines (MMR, varicella) contraindicated in pregnancy; give postpartum

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Weeks 3–8 postconception: organogenesis → malformations; later exposure → growth/functional injury

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ **Alcohol**: poor growth/development, smooth philtrum, thin upper lip, short palpebral fissures

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ **Isotretinoin contraindicated**; pregnancy testing and effective contraception required
Valproate generally avoided when alternatives effective; do not abruptly stop antiseizure drugs
ACE inhibitor → labetalol/nifedipine for pregnancy hypertension; warfarin usually → LMWH

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Prior NTD pregnancy → **folic acid 4 mg/day**, preconception through first trimester
Antiseizure exposure: folate **≥0.4 mg/day**; optimal higher dose uncertain, individualize
Lithium: levels, renal/thyroid tests; early exposure → detailed fetal cardiac assessment

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ No safe alcohol threshold; exposure alone does not mandate pregnancy termination
Mechanical heart valves may require individualized warfarin decisions despite fetal risks
Folate lowers NTD risk but does not erase valproate-associated malformations or developmental harm

table.title: Agent → characteristic fetal injury
rows: Neural tube defects; valproate neurodevelopmental toxicity
Fetal renal injury, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia
Increased cardiac malformation risk, including Ebstein anomaly
Nasal hypoplasia, stippled epiphyses, fetal bleeding
Retinoid-like craniofacial, CNS malformations; reduce supplements

teratogens.evidence: Folate checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/folic-acid/hcp/clinical-overview/), [AAN/AES/SMFM 2024](https://www.aan.com/PressRoom/Home/PressRelease/5170); exposure patterns established pharmacology.

thoracic-trauma.name: Thoracic trauma
thoracic-trauma.scope: Blunt and penetrating chest trauma, blunt cardiac injury, blunt aortic injury, diaphragmatic rupture, pulmonary contusion
thoracic-trauma.core: Chest trauma with respiratory or circulatory compromise requires immediate treatment of life-threatening injuries before definitive imaging.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: High-speed deceleration, steering-wheel impact, crush injuries, penetrating wounds
Lower chest wounds can cross diaphragm and injure abdominal organs

rows.label: Clues
items: Unilateral absent breath sounds, shock, distended neck veins → tension pneumothorax
Flail segment: paradoxical movement; associated lung injury drives hypoxemia
Hypoxemia hours after impact + focal alveolar infiltrate, worsening to 24–48 h, afebrile → **pulmonary contusion**
Left thoracic bowel sounds/loops, **NG tip in left chest**, obscured hemidiaphragm → diaphragmatic rupture

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pleural pressure or pericardial blood impairs venous return → obstructive shock
Alveolar hemorrhage and edema impair gas exchange; rapid deceleration shears the aortic isthmus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Primary survey with **eFAST** and portable chest radiograph; unstable injuries treated clinically
★ Deceleration + **widened mediastinum** → aortic injury; stable → **CT angiography**; normal radiograph cannot exclude
Blunt cardiac injury → ECG and troponin; both normal effectively exclude significant injury
Sternal/anterior rib fractures + new arrhythmia/↑troponin → telemetry; persistent shock → echocardiography
Large persistent air leak, subcutaneous air despite working chest tube → **tracheobronchial rupture**; bronchoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tension pneumothorax → immediate needle/finger decompression → **chest tube**; no imaging delay
Open pneumothorax → vented seal and tube; hemothorax → tube and blood resuscitation
★ Initial tube blood >1500 mL or persistent >200 mL/h → operative exploration
Tamponade with shock/arrest → surgical drainage; pericardiocentesis only temporizing
Contusion/flail chest → oxygen, regional/multimodal analgesia, pulmonary hygiene; intubate for respiratory failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Contusion → ARDS; retained hemothorax → empyema
Rib fractures → splinting, atelectasis, pneumonia; cardiac injury → arrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Seat belts, vehicle safety systems and protective equipment reduce injury risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Myocardial contusion: ventricular ectopy, rising wedge pressure, pulmonary edema after fluids; no pericardial compression
Abdominal hemorrhage: free intraperitoneal fluid; may coexist with thoracic injury
Massive hemothorax: **opacified hemithorax**, flat neck veins; tension pneumothorax: hyperlucent
ARDS: bilateral opacities after 24–48 h; fat embolism: long-bone fracture, petechiae, confusion

thoracic-trauma.evidence: Not checked online; established ATLS-based teaching.

table.title: Definitive associated-injury management
rows: IV esmolol if tolerated; endovascular repair

thrombocytopenia.name: Thrombocytopenia
thrombocytopenia.scope: Evaluation of isolated thrombocytopenia, peripheral smear, immune thrombocytopenia, drug-induced, procedural platelet thresholds
thrombocytopenia.core: Low platelet count requires confirmation and distinction among impaired production, immune destruction, consumption, sequestration, and laboratory artifact.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent infection, autoimmune disease, HIV/HCV, lymphoproliferative disease → secondary immune thrombocytopenia
Heparin, quinine, TMP-SMX, vancomycin; alcohol, marrow-suppressive drugs; cirrhosis with splenic sequestration

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae, purpura, epistaxis, gingival bleeding; mucosal hemorrhage signals clinically important platelet disorder
★ **Neurologic/renal abnormalities + hemolysis** → thrombotic microangiopathy; systemic illness/coagulopathy → DIC
Heparin exposure + >50% platelet decline, thrombosis, typical 5–10-day onset → HIT

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ITP: IgG platelet clearance, impaired megakaryocytes; maternal IgG crosses placenta → **fetal platelet destruction**
Drug-dependent immune destruction often causes abrupt severe counts; HIT: anti-PF4/heparin IgG activates platelets, producing thrombosis
**Kasabach-Merritt**: infant vascular tumor (kaposiform hemangioendothelioma/tufted angioma; older exams: hemangioma) traps platelets → severe thrombocytopenia, consumptive coagulopathy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Repeat CBC + peripheral smear**; platelet clumps → citrate tube for pseudothrombocytopenia
Isolated low platelets, normal coagulation, large platelets → ITP after excluding secondary causes
Schistocytes → LDH, haptoglobin, creatinine, coagulation studies; suspected TTP → urgent ADAMTS13 sample
HIV/HCV testing for new ITP; marrow biopsy only atypical cytopenias or suspected marrow disease
4Ts estimates HIT probability; intermediate/high → PF4 immunoassay, functional confirmation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adult ITP **<30,000/µL or bleeding → glucocorticoid**; children without significant bleeding → observation
★ ITP critical bleeding → **IVIG + high-dose steroid + platelet transfusion**
Drug immune thrombocytopenia → stop culprit; persistent ITP → rituximab, thrombopoietin agonist, or selected splenectomy
Suspected TTP → plasma exchange; HIT → stop heparin, start argatroban/nonheparin anticoagulant
Older board LP target: 50,000/µL; current trigger below; neurosurgical targets often ≥100,000/µL

rows.label: Complications
items: Intracranial hemorrhage with severe disease; thrombosis in HIT/TTP
Steroid toxicity, immunosuppression; splenectomy → encapsulated bacterial sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid culprit rechallenge, aspirin/NSAIDs when bleeding risk high; vaccinate before splenectomy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Von Willebrand disease: often normal platelet count with mucocutaneous bleeding
Marrow failure: additional cytopenias, abnormal precursor morphology

thrombocytopenia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AABB/ICTMG platelet recommendations (2025)](https://www.aabb.org/news-resources/news/article/2025/05/29/aabb-develops-new-platelet-transfusion-guidelines); other hematology principles not separately checked.

transfusion-reactions.name: Transfusion reactions
transfusion-reactions.scope: Acute hemolytic, febrile nonhemolytic, TRALI, TACO, anaphylactic, delayed hemolytic, massive transfusion complications
transfusion-reactions.core: New symptoms during transfusion require stopping the transfusion immediately and evaluating hemolysis, infection and cardiopulmonary compromise.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior transfusion/pregnancy → alloantibodies; IgA deficiency with anti-IgA → anaphylaxis
Heart/kidney failure, rapid infusion, older age → circulatory overload

rows.label: Clues
items: Delayed hemolysis: hemoglobin falls, jaundice days–weeks after compatible transfusion; **DAT positive**, ↑indirect bilirubin
Bacterial contamination: high fever, rigors, profound hypotension; platelets particularly vulnerable
Isolated urticaria without systemic symptoms suggests mild allergic reaction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ABO mismatch → **preformed antibodies** → intravascular complement lysis; anamnestic → delayed extravascular hemolysis
TRALI: inflammatory pulmonary capillary leak; TACO: hydrostatic pressure from excess circulating volume
Febrile nonhemolytic: **cytokines accumulated in stored donor blood**; recipient anti-leukocyte antibodies

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Keep IV access with saline; **recheck patient/unit identity**, notify blood bank
Hemolysis: **DAT** shows coated RBCs; LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin, plasma/urine hemoglobin; send unit/blood samples
Fever/shock → patient and product cultures; dyspnea → chest radiograph, oxygenation, volume assessment
Suspected febrile nonhemolytic reaction remains diagnosis of exclusion after hemolysis/sepsis evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute hemolysis → IV saline, support renal perfusion, treat shock/DIC; **never restart unit**
★ Anaphylaxis → **IM epinephrine**, airway support; future washed or IgA-deficient products
TRALI → supportive oxygen/ventilation; diuretics generally unhelpful unless concomitant overload
TACO → upright positioning, oxygen, **IV furosemide**; slow future transfusions
Contamination → broad IV antibiotics; isolated allergy → diphenhydramine; febrile nonhemolytic → **acetaminophen**

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute hemolysis → AKI, DIC; severe pulmonary reactions → respiratory failure
Massive transfusion → citrate hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia, hypothermia, dilutional thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Bedside identification and crossmatch; leukoreduction reduces febrile reactions
Massive hemorrhage → balanced blood components, temperature and ionized calcium monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Underlying sepsis: symptoms may precede infusion; cultures clarify
Aspiration: event-linked infiltrate without transfusion-specific mechanism

transfusion-reactions.evidence: Not checked online; established transfusion-medicine definitions.

traumatic-brain-injury.name: Traumatic brain injury
traumatic-brain-injury.scope: Epidural hematoma, subdural hematoma, cerebral contusion, diffuse axonal injury, concussion, elevated ICP
traumatic-brain-injury.core: Head trauma ranges from transient functional disturbance to expanding hemorrhage; serial neurologic deterioration requires urgent imaging and neurosurgical assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Falls, crashes, assault, sports; anticoagulants, antiplatelets, bleeding disorders
Older age, alcohol use and cerebral atrophy predispose to bridging-vein injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Headache, vomiting, amnesia; focal deficit or progressive somnolence suggests structural injury; hemiparesis → contralateral supratentorial mass
★ **Unilateral fixed dilated pupil + declining consciousness** → uncal herniation
Cushing response: hypertension, bradycardia, irregular breathing; late sign of ↑ICP

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impact/shear → ischemia, excitotoxicity; **cerebral edema** → deterioration over 1–3 days, brainstem reflex loss
Rising intracranial volume → ↓cerebral perfusion; hypotension/hypoxia worsen secondary injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ ABCs/cervical protection → **GCS, pupils, focal examination**, repeated serially
**Noncontrast head CT** for moderate/severe injury or mild injury with high-risk features
High-risk features: anticoagulation, skull-fracture signs, focal deficit, repeated vomiting, worsening symptoms
GCS 13–15 mild, 9–12 moderate, ≤8 severe

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **GCS ≤8 or hypoventilation → intubate before imaging/surgery**; avoid hypoxemia/hypotension; reverse anticoagulants
Expanding hematoma, mass effect or deterioration → urgent neurosurgical evacuation
★ Elevated ICP → head elevation, analgesia/sedation, **hypertonic saline or mannitol**; treat sustained ICP >22 mm Hg
Herniation → brief hyperventilation as bridge; no prophylactic hyperventilation or corticosteroids
Severe/high-risk TBI → levetiracetam for 7 days; refractory ICP → neurosurgical decompression

rows.label: Complications
items: Posttraumatic seizures, chronic cognitive/behavioral impairment, postconcussion syndrome, hydrocephalus
Skull-base fracture → CSF leak/meningitis; no nasal instrumentation
Frontal contusion → **executive dysfunction**: impaired conceptual planning, judgment, motivation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Seatbelts, helmets, fall prevention
Concussion: no same-day sports; relative rest 24–48 hours → graded recovery
Persistent symptoms, even normal CT → **no contact sports** until reassessed; second-impact risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Intoxication: may coexist; exclude intracranial injury first
Hypoglycemia: check glucose in any altered mental status

table.title: Injury patterns
rows: Temporal impact; middle meningeal artery; lucid interval
Bridging-vein rupture; acute or weeks-later fluctuating decline
Crescent; crosses sutures, limited by dural reflections
Immediate prolonged coma after rotational acceleration
Transient LOC, amnesia, headache, vomiting; normal neurologic exam

traumatic-brain-injury.evidence: Acute management checked 2026-10-30: [ACS TBI best practices, 2024](https://www.facs.org/media/vgfgjpfk/best-practices-guidelines-traumatic-brain-injury.pdf).

type-2-diabetes-mellitus.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Diagnosis, glycemic targets, pharmacotherapy (metformin contraindications, SGLT2i, GLP-1 RA, insulin), chronic complications screening, pediatric screening in obesity
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.core: Insulin resistance with progressive beta-cell failure produces chronic hyperglycemia and vascular injury, often preceding obvious symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Central obesity, family history, prior gestational diabetes, PCOS, physical inactivity
Glucocorticoids and atypical antipsychotics can unmask dysglycemia

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, recurrent candidiasis; acanthosis nigricans suggests marked insulin resistance
Weight loss, ketosis, or dehydration → severe insulin deficiency; reconsider diabetes type

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired glucose uptake + excess hepatic output; early compensatory **↑serum insulin**, later relative secretory failure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **A1c ≥6.5%**, fasting glucose ≥126, or 2-hour OGTT ≥200 mg/dL
Random glucose ≥200 with classic symptoms also diagnostic; otherwise confirm with second abnormal result
A1c unreliable with altered erythrocyte survival; use plasma glucose
★ Youth: screen puberty/age 10, whichever earlier, with overweight/obesity + additional risk; repeat ≥every 2 years

rows.label: Tx
items: Lifestyle + metformin; **lactic acidosis**: avoid eGFR <30, AKI/sepsis, hypoxia; no new start <45; reduce 30–44
★ HF/CKD → **SGLT2 inhibitor**; ASCVD/obesity → GLP-1 RA, independent of A1c or metformin
★ Catabolism, glucose ≥300, or A1c >10% → **insulin**
Otherwise GLP-1 RA before insulin; older exam questions may expect **basal insulin** once two orals fail
Adults: A1c <7%, fasting 80–130, postmeal <180; relax for frailty/hypoglycemia; quarterly checks until stable

rows.label: Complications
items: Retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, foot ulceration; coronary, cerebral, and peripheral arterial disease
SGLT2 inhibitors: genital mycoses, euglycemic DKA; sulfonylureas/insulin: hypoglycemia, weight gain
Metformin: GI intolerance, B12 deficiency; pioglitazone: edema, HF; sulfonylureas: labeled caution with sulfa allergy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ At diagnosis then annually: **urine albumin/creatinine, eGFR, foot and dilated eye examinations** (eye spacing by findings)
★ Albuminuria + hypertension → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**, never both; efferent dilation ↓intraglomerular pressure
BP ≥130/80 → antihypertensive; older exam questions may expect ACE inhibitor, also normotensive albuminuria
Statin age 40–75; glycemic control slows **neuropathy**, retinopathy, nephropathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Type 1 diabetes: autoantibodies, low C-peptide, abrupt ketosis
Diabetes insipidus: dilute polyuria without elevated blood glucose

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery/radiation suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stress: aging/multiparity weaken pelvic floor → **urethral hypermobility**, low sphincter tone
Urge: **uninhibited detrusor contractions** (detrusor instability), worsened by caffeine; MS lesion → low residual
Overflow: **detrusor underactivity/acontractile bladder** (MS, diabetes, stroke) or outlet obstruction → high residual
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
**Q-tip excursion >30°** on Valsalva → urethral hypermobility (urethrocele)
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic (oxybutynin); discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

urticaria.name: Urticaria
urticaria.scope: acute vs chronic urticaria, triggers, pathophysiology (mast cell degranulation), second-generation H1 antihistamines, workup indications
urticaria.core: Transient pruritic wheals from mast-cell mediator release; each lesion resolves within 24 hours, while recurrent episodes may continue for weeks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Acute: viral illness, foods, medications, insect stings; NSAIDs can provoke or worsen episodes
Chronic spontaneous disease often idiopathic/autoimmune; cold, pressure, heat or exercise trigger inducible forms

rows.label: Clues
items: Raised blanching erythematous plaques with pale centers; migratory distribution, no residual scar
Angioedema may accompany wheals: deeper eyelid/lip swelling, lasting longer than superficial lesions
★ **Wheals + wheeze, hypotension, stridor or gastrointestinal symptoms** → possible anaphylaxis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Histamine and other mast-cell mediators cause superficial dermal edema and itch
Drug/food exposure, minutes to hours → **type I IgE** degranulation; T-cell (type IV) rashes take days
Chronic spontaneous disease rarely reflects hidden food allergy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; acute <6 weeks, chronic ≥6 weeks; detailed exposure and medication history
Uncomplicated acute disease → no routine tests; chronic → limited CBC/differential, ESR/CRP ± targeted thyroid assessment
★ **Painful lesion >24 hours, bruising/purpura or systemic findings** → biopsy for urticarial vasculitis
Reproducible exposure → targeted allergy testing; no indiscriminate food panels, infection screens or malignancy searches

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Cetirizine, fexofenadine or loratadine** daily; chronic uncontrolled disease → increase up to fourfold
Antihistamine-resistant chronic disease → **omalizumab**; refractory → specialist-directed cyclosporine
Anaphylaxis → **IM epinephrine immediately**, airway/circulatory support; antihistamines do not replace epinephrine
Severe short exacerbation → brief oral corticosteroid course sometimes; avoid long-term systemic steroids
Stop culprit; avoid routine sedating antihistamines because of cognitive/anticholinergic effects

rows.label: Complications
items: Sleep disruption, impaired quality of life, anxiety; airway compromise when associated with systemic allergy
Cold urticaria with cold-water immersion → systemic reaction or drowning

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid confirmed triggers and aggravating NSAIDs; temperature/pressure adjustments for inducible disease
Document serious drug allergy; epinephrine autoinjector for patients with anaphylaxis risk, not every isolated wheal

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contact dermatitis: fixed eczematous lesions lasting days, exposure distribution
Urticarial vasculitis: painful fixed plaques, residual bruising, possible renal/joint disease
Bradykinin angioedema: swelling without itch/wheals; ACE inhibitor exposure or C1-inhibitor deficiency

vaginitis.name: Vaginitis
vaginitis.scope: Bacterial vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Vulvovaginal candidiasis, atrophic vaginitis, genitourinary syndrome of menopause
vaginitis.core: Vaginal discharge or irritation requires distinction among dysbiosis, sexually transmitted protozoal infection, yeast overgrowth, and hypoestrogenic mucosal change.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: BV: new partners, douching; trichomoniasis: sexual exposure
Candida: antibiotics, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression; atrophy: menopause or other hypoestrogenic states
Prepubertal: hand inoculation of respiratory pathogens during URI

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus, dysuria, dyspareunia; discharge appearance overlaps, so symptoms alone insufficient
★ **Fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness** → evaluate PID rather than isolated vaginitis
Postmenopausal bleeding needs assessment beyond assuming atrophy
★ Prepubertal **foul purulent/bloody discharge** → retained vaginal **foreign body**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: BV: lactobacilli depleted, anaerobes expand; Candida causes inflammatory overgrowth
Low estrogen thins epithelium and reduces lactobacilli → mucosal fragility and elevated vaginal pH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Vaginal pH, saline/KOH microscopy**, history and examination; NAAT improves infectious diagnosis
BV: ≥3 Amsel—discharge, ↑pH, clue cells, amine odor; Gardnerella culture unhelpful (normal flora)
★ Suspected trichomoniasis + negative wet mount → **NAAT**, not reassurance
Recurrent/complicated Candida → culture or PCR for species; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **oral metronidazole 7 days in women**; treat partners, abstain until completed/resolved
BV → oral metronidazole 7 days or vaginal metronidazole/clindamycin, **no routine partner treatment**, ACOG: treat if recurrent; treat symptomatic pregnancy
Candida → topical azole/nystatin or oral fluconazole; **pregnancy: topical azole 7 days**, avoid oral fluconazole
GSM → moisturizers/lubricants, then low-dose vaginal estrogen for persistent symptoms
Recurrent BV: ACOG 2025 considers male-partner metronidazole + topical clindamycin; older boards omit

rows.label: Complications
items: BV/trichomoniasis associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and increased STI acquisition
Recurrent symptoms → reassess diagnosis, adherence, reinfection, diabetes or resistant/non-albicans yeast

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **retest women at about 3 months**; condoms
Avoid douching/irritants; no routine partner treatment for uncomplicated Candida

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: endocervical mucopus, friability, positive GC/CT NAAT
Contact dermatitis: external irritation after product exposure
Sarcoma botryoides: girl with bleeding, grape-like polypoid vaginal mass

valvular-heart-disease.name: Valvular heart disease
valvular-heart-disease.scope: Aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, mitral stenosis, mitral regurgitation, mitral valve prolapse, physical exam, echocardiography, surgical and transcatheter replacement
valvular-heart-disease.core: Murmur timing, location, radiation, and loading maneuvers localize valve disease; symptoms and ventricular response determine intervention.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Trileaflet calcification, age >70 → AS; rheumatic disease → MS
Bicuspid valve: murmur from youth, premature calcific AS (40s–60s); childhood **endocarditis**; adult aortic dissection
AR: endocarditis, dissection, **root dilation** (Marfan, hypertension; murmur along right sternal border)
MR: ischemia, myxomatous prolapse (connective tissue laxity), chamber dilation

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, pulmonary edema, reduced exercise tolerance; abrupt deterioration suggests acute regurgitation
★ **Exertional syncope, angina, or HF** with obstruction → severe symptomatic disease
Squatting/handgrip increase regurgitant murmurs; standing/Valsalva → earlier MVP click, squatting → later

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stenosis produces upstream pressure overload; regurgitation produces chamber volume overload
Acute regurgitation lacks compensatory dilation, rapidly elevating filling pressures and reducing forward output
Mitral stenosis: ↑LA pressure, ↑PCWP, ↑pulmonary artery pressure; **LVEDP normal**; AF abolishes presystolic accentuation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TTE Doppler** defines anatomy, severity, EF, chamber dimensions, pulmonary pressures
Severe AS: velocity ≥4 m/s, mean gradient ≥40, or valve area ≤1 cm²; discordance requires reassessment
Severe MS: valve area ≤1.5 cm²; TEE for thrombus before balloon intervention or uncertain anatomy
★ Acute murmur with shock → **urgent echocardiography**; TEE if endocarditis/dissection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe AR/MR → **urgent surgery**, stabilize with afterload reduction/diuresis if BP permits
Severe primary MR: **EF ≤60% or LVESD ≥40 mm** triggers intervention even without symptoms
Secondary MR → optimize HF treatment first; selected persistent severe cases benefit from transcatheter edge-to-edge repair
Avoid excessive preload reduction in severe AS; symptomatic relief never replaces needed valve intervention

rows.label: Complications
items: Heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, AF, systemic embolism, endocarditis
Mechanical prosthesis: thrombosis/bleeding; bioprosthesis: structural degeneration
Prosthetic dysfunction/paravalvular leak → new murmur, **schistocytes**, hemolytic anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Warfarin for mechanical valves**; no DOAC substitution; rheumatic MS with AF also requires warfarin
Prosthetic valve or prior endocarditis → selected dental prophylaxis; native isolated MVP does not qualify
Periodic echo and symptom review; treat rheumatic fever to prevent recurrent valve injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: HCM: systolic murmur increases with Valsalva/standing
Aortic sclerosis: ejection murmur without significant gradient; flow murmur: normal valve anatomy

table.title: Valve signatures and definitive options
rows: Crescendo-decrescendo, carotids; soft A2; pulsus parvus et tardus
Early diastolic decrescendo; wide pulse pressure
Loud S1, opening snap, apical mid-diastolic rumble
Suitable symptomatic rheumatic valve → balloon commissurotomy
LLSB holosystolic, louder on inspiration; right HF

valvular-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established echo thresholds and intervention framework.

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, inherited thrombophilia
**Previous VTE** is the strongest predictor of recurrence; remote surgery months ago adds little
**Central venous catheter** → main cause of upper-extremity DVT

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload
Massive PE: high RA/PA pressure, low PCWP, low output; RV infarct: PA pressure normal/low

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week
Low-probability V/Q + high clinical suspicion is nondiagnostic → **CT angiography**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; cancer → LMWH/DOAC; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible
Acute proximal DVT/PE without DOAC → immediate **heparin**; warfarin alone never initial; inferior in cancer

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Aspirin or 1 month inadequate; DOACs now preferred, older exam questions may expect warfarin 3–6 months
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization
Hip arthroplasty → LMWH, warfarin or DOAC; aspirin now accepted, older exam questions may expect anticoagulant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome
Amniotic fluid embolism: peripartum collapse with **DIC/low fibrinogen**

table.title: Treatment branches; 2026 PE guidance uses categories A–E
rows: Stable; low PESI/sPESI; no RV injury
Normotensive + RV dysfunction and/or troponin elevation
Sustained SBP <90 mm Hg or shock

viral-hepatitis.name: Viral hepatitis
viral-hepatitis.scope: Hepatitis A, B, C, D, E, serologic markers, acute vs chronic hepatitis, HCV antibody and RNA confirmatory testing, direct-acting antivirals, postexposure prophylaxis (HBIG and vaccine)
viral-hepatitis.core: Hepatocellular injury with malaise, anorexia, jaundice, and high aminotransferases prompts exposure-based viral testing; chronic infection may be clinically silent.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HAV/HEV: fecal–oral spread; HBV/HCV/HDV: blood, perinatal exposure; HBV also sexual
Injection exposure, unscreened blood, endemic birth region; HDV requires HBV
HEV severe in pregnancy; perinatal HBV and most untreated HCV often become chronic

rows.label: Clues
items: Dark urine, pale stool, RUQ discomfort; transaminases often far exceed alkaline phosphatase
★ **Encephalopathy + INR ≥1.5 without preexisting cirrhosis** → acute liver failure
HBV: serum sickness, polyarteritis nodosa; HCV: mixed cryoglobulinemia, porphyria cutanea tarda

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Host immune injury to infected hepatocytes; persistent HBV/HCV → fibrosis and carcinogenesis
HBV nuclear templates persist; HCV cure does not confer immunity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ HAV acute → **IgM anti-HAV**; total/IgG antibody indicates immunity
★ **HCV antibody → reflex HCV RNA**; antibody persists after clearance; recent exposure → RNA directly
HBsAg persisting >6 months → chronic HBV; HBV DNA quantifies replication
HEV testing by exposure/context; HBsAg-positive severe hepatitis → consider anti-HDV/HDV RNA
INR, bilirubin, creatinine; chronic disease → fibrosis staging, coinfection testing

rows.label: Tx
items: HAV, most HEV, uncomplicated acute HBV → supportive care; liver failure → urgent transplant center
★ Chronic HCV → **glecaprevir/pibrentasvir or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir**, usually 8–12 weeks; verify interactions/cirrhosis
Chronic HBV needing treatment → tenofovir or entecavir; severe acute HBV also may need antiviral
HCV cure: RNA undetectable ≥12 weeks after completion; do not delay treatment awaiting spontaneous resolution

rows.label: Complications
items: Fulminant hepatitis; chronic HBV/HCV → cirrhosis, portal hypertension, hepatocellular carcinoma
HBV can cause HCC without cirrhosis; DAAs may reactivate unrecognized HBV
Cirrhosis/selected HBV → HCC surveillance with ultrasound ± AFP every 6 months

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Susceptible HBV exposure → **HBIG + vaccine promptly**, preferably within 24 h; immunity determines exceptions
Newborn ≥2,000 g, maternal HBsAg unknown → vaccine ≤12 h; HBIG only if mother positive
HAV exposure ≤2 weeks → vaccine; add immune globulin for immunocompromise/chronic liver disease
HAV/HBV vaccines, safer sex/injection practices; no HCV vaccine or proven HCV PEP

rows.label: Mimics
items: Drug-induced injury: medication/toxin relationship
Ischemic hepatitis: shock preceding abrupt marked aminotransferase rise

vulvar-cancer.name: Vulvar cancer
vulvar-cancer.scope: Squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma of the vulva, lichen sclerosus malignant transformation, vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN), Paget disease of the vulva, staging, wide local excision, sentinel node biopsy
vulvar-cancer.core: Persistent vulvar pruritus with a focal ulcer, plaque, or mass requires biopsy, especially in an older patient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HPV-related disease: smoking, immunosuppression; HPV-independent disease: older age, lichen sclerosus
Prior vulvar HSIL/VIN; chronic symptoms repeatedly treated without tissue diagnosis delay detection
Prior cervical neoplasia: HPV field risk; new vulvar mass → primary cancer, metastasis rare

rows.label: Clues
items: Nonhealing lesion, bleeding, dyspareunia, focal pain; enlarged inguinal nodes suggest regional spread
★ **Changing pigmented lesion** requires melanoma evaluation; amelanotic lesions also occur

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Squamous carcinoma spreads locally, then to inguinofemoral nodes; nodal involvement strongly influences prognosis
HPV-associated HSIL and HPV-independent differentiated VIN are distinct precursor pathways

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Punch/incisional biopsy** of suspicious lesion; sample viable edge, not only necrotic center
Document lesion size, depth, focality, proximity to midline; examine groin nodes
Suspicious nodes → ultrasound-guided sampling; advanced local extent → pelvic MRI and metastatic imaging
Stage by stromal invasion, adjacent-organ extension, and nodal/distant spread; evaluate multifocal disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive disease → **wide local excision** with negative margins
Microinvasive SCC ≤1 mm stromal invasion generally needs no groin-node surgery
★ Unifocal **<4 cm**, invasion >1 mm, clinically negative nodes → sentinel-node biopsy
Larger/multifocal or node-positive disease → groin treatment; locally advanced → chemoradiation and/or surgery
Paget → excision; VIN → excision, or laser/imiquimod after excluding invasion

rows.label: Complications
items: Local recurrence, nodal metastasis; surgery/radiation → lymphedema, wound breakdown, sexual dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: HPV vaccination, tobacco cessation; high-potency topical corticosteroids for lichen sclerosus, continued surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lichen simplex chronicus: diffuse scratch-induced thickening; biopsy persistent focal changes
Candidiasis: yeast on microscopy, responds to antifungal; persistent lesion still needs sampling

table.title: Histologic clues
rows: Ulcerated/keratotic mass; HPV or inflammatory pathway
Asymmetry, irregular color/border; Breslow depth guides management
Chronic eczematous red plaque; intraepithelial glandular cells

vulvar-cancer.evidence: Excision/node selection checked 2026-10-30: [NCI PDQ](https://www.cancer.gov/types/vulvar/hp/vulvar-treatment-pdq); remaining pathology established teaching.

wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.name: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.scope: Wernicke encephalopathy (triad of encephalopathy, ataxia, oculomotor dysfunction), Korsakoff psychosis (confabulation, amnesia), thiamine (B1) deficiency, IV thiamine before glucose, mammillary body atrophy
wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.core: Malnourished adult with confusion, gait ataxia, or ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus; the complete Wernicke triad is often absent.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Alcohol use disorder, hyperemesis gravidarum, bariatric surgery, starvation, inadequate parenteral nutrition
IV dextrose, carbohydrate loading or refeeding increases thiamine demand → precipitates Wernicke in depleted patients

rows.label: Clues
items: Ocular: nystagmus, **bilateral lateral rectus (CN VI) palsy**, conjugate-gaze palsy; wide-based gait
Hypothermia, hypotension, or coma signal severe deficiency
★ Korsakoff: disproportionate **anterograde amnesia**, retrograde memory loss, confabulation; relatively preserved alertness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Thiamine deficiency impairs carbohydrate metabolism → ATP failure and selective neuronal injury
Medial thalami, periaqueductal gray, mammillary bodies injured → persistent amnestic syndrome

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; do not wait for vitamin assays or imaging before treatment
MRI may show symmetric thalamic/periaqueductal lesions; normal MRI does not exclude Wernicke
Chronic disease: mammillary body atrophy; evaluate glucose, electrolytes, magnesium, and competing encephalopathy causes

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected Wernicke → **high-dose IV thiamine**, followed by oral replacement after stabilization
**IV thiamine before or with dextrose**, hypoglycemia included; if thiamine unavailable, never delay dextrose
Replete magnesium, fluid/electrolyte deficits; restore nutrition cautiously and treat alcohol withdrawal separately
Ocular findings may improve rapidly; gait/cognition recover more slowly; established amnesia often persists

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated encephalopathy → death or irreversible Korsakoff syndrome; falls and impaired independent living
Refeeding syndrome → hypophosphatemia, arrhythmias, respiratory weakness

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Routine oral **thiamine supplementation** for persistent malnutrition; nutritional assessment during alcohol treatment
Alcohol cessation support, balanced nutrition; monitor intake after bariatric surgery or prolonged vomiting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcohol withdrawal delirium: autonomic hyperactivity, tremor, hallucinations after reduced intake
Hepatic encephalopathy: cirrhosis, asterixis, precipitating bleed or infection
Posterior circulation stroke: abrupt focal deficits; diffusion MRI identifies infarction

wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.evidence: Not checked online; established thiamine-deficiency teaching.

wrist-and-hand-injuries.name: Wrist and hand injuries
wrist-and-hand-injuries.scope: Scaphoid fracture, distal radius fracture (Colles), boxer fracture, gamekeeper thumb, de Quervain tenosynovitis
wrist-and-hand-injuries.core: Mechanism and focal anatomy guide hand injury care; normal initial radiographs do not exclude a clinically important occult fracture.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fall on outstretched hand → carpal/distal radius injury; osteoporosis increases fragility-fracture risk
Closed-fist strike → fifth metacarpal; forced thumb abduction → ulnar collateral ligament injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Focal swelling, bruising, deformity, reduced grip; compare cascade and rotation with fingers flexed
★ **Numb thumb/index/middle fingers** after wrist trauma → acute median compression
Open wound, severe passive-stretch pain, pallor, or tense swelling → urgent surgical evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Carpal vascular supply and ligament stability determine ischemia/nonunion risk after injury
Displaced bone or swelling can compress nerves; rotational deformity disproportionately impairs hand function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AP/lateral/oblique radiographs**; dedicated scaphoid views for suspected occult carpal fracture
Neurovascular and tendon examination before/after reduction; document capillary refill, sensation, motor function
★ **Scaphoid suspicion despite negative films** → **immobilize**, repeat in 10–14 days or early MRI
Lateral wrist view assesses carpal alignment; thumb stress instability may require radiograph/ultrasound or MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Displacement/dislocation → **analgesia, reduction, splint**; instability/neurovascular compromise → urgent orthopedics
Thumb UCL complete tear/Stener lesion → repair; partial stable tear → thumb immobilization
Inspect knuckle wounds: fight bite → irrigation, amoxicillin-clavulanate, hand-surgery evaluation if deep
Remove rings early; open fracture → sterile dressing, IV cefazolin, tetanus assessment, urgent debridement

rows.label: Complications
items: ★ Scaphoid proximal pole → **avascular necrosis/nonunion**; missed carpal dislocation → chronic instability/arthritis
Malrotation, stiffness, tendon injury, complex regional pain syndrome; Colles fracture may cause delayed extensor rupture

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protective sports equipment, fall prevention, osteoporosis evaluation after low-trauma fracture
Early finger motion when safe; splint-care counseling and reassessment for increasing pain/numbness

rows.label: Mimics
items: De Quervain tenosynovitis: first dorsal compartment; radial styloid pain with Finkelstein, no acute bony injury
Carpal tunnel syndrome: chronic nocturnal symptoms without traumatic deformity
Septic flexor tenosynovitis: fusiform digit, flexed posture, sheath tenderness, passive-extension pain

wrist-and-hand-injuries.evidence: Not checked online; established hand-injury diagnosis and stabilization.
